The Commonwealth Games might be the only sporting event for which the most-Googled terms are asking what they are and why they exist. One of the top stories on BBC Sport at the time of writing was simply headlined: “What are the Commonwealth Games?”

It’s a good question. They are an anachronistic idea, vaguely defined, thinly justified, a relic of our imperial past, like a mildly offensive heirloom quadrennially hauled down from the attic, modern sport’s unwelcome inheritance from another age.

So yes, the so-called Friendly Games are clearly a little unloved, given the battle to find a willing host. They were tossed aside by Melbourne before a stripped-back version was salvaged by Glasgow, a rescue Games.

They are not fully respected, given not all the stars will show up over the next 10 days. Keely Hodgkinson is prioritising other events. Canadian sensation Summer McIntosh is focused on the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships, preferring to compete against serious American rivals rather than a bunch of island nations.

The Games might even be hard to find, given they are behind a paywall on TNT Sports in the UK, with only highlights on Channel 5.

But dig under the surface and there is history here. The Games were the scene of the “Miracle Mile”, an epic contest between Roger Bannister and John Landy when both broke the four-minute barrier; they were the stage on which a 15-year-old Ian Thorpe announced himself to the world, where Adam Peaty broke new ground, where Eilish McColgan made history rhyme 30 years after her mum won the same race.

And if the weight of history doesn’t imbue the modern Commonwealth Games in quite the same way, then perhaps there is something easy and compelling about sport with relatively low stakes, sport that has little commercial pretence, naked sport that’s all the more human for it. There will be no political interference here, no dynamic pricing strategy, no advertising masquerading as essential hydration. Thanks to the Boston Tea Party, there will be no Americans either.

open image in gallery The Commonwealth Games has plenty of entertaining sport on offer ( Getty/The Independent )

The Commonwealth Games’ days may be numbered, like county cricket or League Cup semi-final second legs, but perhaps that’s one reason to settle in and watch this jumble of sport. You don’t know what you have until it’s gone, and quite frankly, we will probably never get lawn bowls at the Olympics.

Here are 11 more reasons to embrace the Games this summer.

The Commonwealth Mile

It is a event unique to the Commonwealth Games: a mile run around the track, which replaces the 1500m this year.

The Mile is back on the schedule after 60 years away, last being run at the 1966 Games in Kingston, Jamaica, before athletics went metric. It is partly a celebration of the Games’ heritage and also a nod to the famous Miracle Mile race between Bannister and Landy.

World Athletics president Seb Coe – a mile record holder in his day – pushed for the change, saying the imperial distance holds a cultural significance in many Commonwealth countries and the race itself carries a certain mystique and prestige. It is the “quintessential Commonwealth athletics event”, Coe said.

It just so happens that Scotland’s home hero Josh Kerr broke the long-standing mile record last week, and Kerr – one of the faces of these Glasgow Games – will be back in action to try and go even quicker than his stunning mark of 3min 42.66sec. He will be up against fellow Scot and former 1500m world champion Jake Wightman.

open image in gallery An exhausted Roger Bannister after beating John Landy in the Mircale Mile ( Getty )

Scotland

Scotland won the unofficial fans’ World Cup in North America this summer with their non-stop partying in Boston and Miami, and while the Commonwealth Games will be a quieter affair, local fans are expected to turn out in force to support their athletes and make a buzz inside the venues.

Don’t expect renditions of “Yes Sir, I Can Boogie”, but we’ll hear “Flower of Scotland” whenever a home athlete wins gold, which will be a regular occurrence: the Scots expect to finish near the top of the medal table, up there with Australia, England, Canada and India.

Incidentally, Finnie the unicorn, the Games’ mascot, has a traffic cone for a horn.

open image in gallery Finne the unicorn is the Commonwealth Games mascot ( Getty )

Kanyinsola Ajayi

Ajayi could be the next great sprinter in men’s athletics, and he is expected to show exactly why there is so much excitement when he goes for 100m gold in Glasgow over the coming days.

The Nigerian 21-year-old was eliminated in the 100m semi-finals at the Paris Olympics two years ago, and finished sixth in the World Championship final last September.

Ajayi has since risen to the top with two hugely impressive Diamond League victories in recent weeks, running 9.84sec in both Prefontaine and London, clinching the latter with a cheeky stare across the finish line at world champion Oblique Seville beside him. Seville will be in Glasgow to gain revenge in their brewing rivalry, but Ajayi has proven he has the speed to back up the bravado.

Gentle nationalism

If you ignore the strong smell of colonialism that lingers around these Games, then you can find a kind of warm patriotism that comes to the fore here. One of the unique parts of the Commonwealth Games is that they offer athletes the chance to represent their piece of the UK, whether that’s Wales, the Isle of Man or Guernsey – and each offers a better national anthem than “God Save the King” (England adopted “Jerusalem” in 2010).

Commonwealth athletes talk of relishing the unique platform for their relatively small sporting communities to march under their own flag and punch above their weight on an international stage. The African nation of Eswatini, for example, has never won a medal at the Olympics but has enjoyed three moments of national pride at the Commonwealth Games over the years. We are still waiting for the Pacific island nation of Tokelau (population: 2,691) to send a competitor.

open image in gallery Eswatini parade in the Commonwealth Games opening ceremony at Birmingham 2022 ( Getty Images )

Bowls

A staple of the Commonwealth Games schedule is lawn bowls, a quaint game that has a similar effect to curling during the Winter Olympics when, for a week or so every four years, the UK becomes a nation of aficionados. This year the event is being staged indoors rather than on grass for logistical reasons, so it’s just bowls.

Look out for the legendary Alex ‘Tattie’ Marshall, Scotland’s most decorated Commonwealth Games athlete, competing in his sixth here. He gained fame for an enthusiastic celebration when beating England in 2014. Marshall’s 23-year-old niece, Beth Riva, will also be in action on the bowling floor.

open image in gallery Alex Marshall, centre, is back in Glasgow for another Commonwealth Games, 12 years after the last ( Getty )

Duncan Scott

One of the faces of the Games will no doubt be Scott, a Scot, and a hugely popular swimmer who has been an Olympic, world, European and Commonwealth champion, and an essential part of Britain’s relay success over the past decade. His career has been one of passionate highs and frustrating near-misses: all four of his individual Olympic medals are silver.

Scott, who was born in Glasgow, is expected to go for glory in freestyle, medley and butterfly events, and he will get the decibels rising around the pool every time he competes.

open image in gallery Duncan Scott will receive plenty of adulation in Glasgow ( Getty )

Para-sport

The Commonwealth Games folds its para-events in with the rest of the action, and that makes for a more inclusive event that provides a greater showcase for some of the stars on show. There will be plenty to enjoy this summer, including athletics, bowls, powerlifting, swimming, track cycling and wheelchair basketball.

The latter is always entertaining, played in the more fast-paced, loud 3v3 format rather than the five-a-side Paralympic format. England are aiming to go better than their bronze medals in the men’s and women’s events four years ago, but to do so they will have to overcome either Australia or Canada, who contested both finals – Australia won the men’s, Canada won the women’s.

open image in gallery Australia won men's wheelchair basketball gold at Birmingham 2022 ( Getty )

England’s breaststroke duel

One of the big storylines in the pool will be men’s breaststroke. The greatest of all time, now Adam Ramsay-Peaty after his recent wedding with Gordon Ramsay’s daughter Holly, announced himself on the big stage at the 2014 Commonwealths in Glasgow, and the 31-year-old is back where it started as he chases his ultimate goal of reclaiming his Olympic 100m title in Los Angeles in 2028.

But Ramsay-Peaty faces competition from the teenage prodigy breaking the veteran’s youth records: Jersey’s Filip Kowacki. The 18-year-old Kowacki is one of Britain’s brightest prospects for LA in a couple of years. Here, Kowacki will try to deliver Jersey’s first Commonwealth medal since 1990 by taking down his idol.

open image in gallery Adam Ramsay-Peaty in training ahead of the start of the Commonwealth Games ( Getty )

Women’s track showdown

Dina Asher-Smith and Daryll Neita will carry English hopes against a stacked line-up from the Caribbean, including Olympic 100m champion Julien Alfred from St Lucia, Jamaica’s double 200m world champion Shericka Jackson, and Alana Reid, who at 21 is tipped to be Jamaica’s next great sprint queen.

open image in gallery Julien Alfred is the Olympic champion over 100m ( Getty )

Velodrome speed

There will be a whole raft of entertainment on offer in the Sir Chris Hoy velodrome over the coming days, including the exploits of Emma Finucane, one of Wales’ great hopes at these Games after winning three medals in Paris including Olympic gold as part of GB’s sprint team. There will be interest in her partner too, Matt Richardson, who caused a stir in the cycling world when he swapped allegiance from Australia to England.

open image in gallery Team GB celebrate gold at the Olympics in Paris ( David Davies/PA Wire )

Rising stars

The Commonwealth Games always proves to be a stage for young talent to come to the fore, and this summer will be no different. Some of the stars of LA ‘28 will be gaining valuable experience in Glasgow and will show their talent at a major multi-sport event for the first time.

There is a deep pool of rising stars to watch, but look out for England’s diminutive boxer Ruby White, 19, ​​a four-time European champion who has been tipped for a medal; and the Carroll sisters, who both have visual impairment and will be competing against one another in the para-swimming competition. Astrid, 17, will represent Scotland while Ursula, 14, will swim for England.

Shania Twain turned down an invitation to Taylor Swift’s wedding in New York City to perform with Harry Styles, Swift’s ex-boyfriend, at Wembley stadium.

Twain, 60, opened for Styles during his 12-night London residency, which ran from 12 June to 4 July as part of his Together, Together tour.

That meant that she was unable to attend Swift’s wedding to Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden on 3 July.

Twain said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that she was “very honoured” to be invited to the wedding.

“Next time I see her, I will of course give her a big congratulations,” she said.

“I admire her musicianship and her commitment to telling her stories, I love her.”

open image in gallery Shania Twain, left, Ciara and Taylor Swift onstage during the 2019 American Music Awards ( Getty )

Swift and Twain have been friends for years, and the “Opalite” singer often cites the country legend as an inspiration.

Styles, 32, and Swift, 36, dated from 2012 to 2013.

Prior to the Wembley shows, Twain had performed with Styles at Coachella in 2022 and the Brit Awards in 2023.

Speaking about how they met, she said: “I met Harry backstage at a very small show, and we chatted for a little bit.

“He was still just getting going, he wasn’t the Harry he is now.

“We exchanged numbers and he called me a little bit later and said, ‘it’s my mum’s birthday coming up, would you mind wishing her a happy birthday because she’s the person who introduced me to your music?’”

Twain sang happy birthday to Styles’s mother over the phone and the two singers kept in touch.

open image in gallery Shania Twain and Taylor Swift, pictured in 2011 ( Getty )

The Canadian singer appeared on the talk show to promote her new album, Little Miss Twain, which will be released on 24 July.

Swift and Kelce reportedly had 1,000 guests at their wedding, with celebrities including Gigi Hadid and Bradley Cooper, Graham Norton, Ed Sheeran, Hugh Grant and Ethan Hawke all in attendance.

Their romance began in 2023 after Kelce publicly announced on his podcast that he was interested in Swift, which she later said was a “wild, romantic gesture”.

In October 2025, Swift made her first TV appearance on Graham Norton’s BBC talk show since her engagement, where she jokingly told the host she was planning on inviting “anyone I’ve ever talked to” to her wedding.

Styles is currently in a relationship with Zoe Kravitz, who he was first linked to in August 2025.

When 72-year-old Michael Roper rides his bicycle to and from the pub he owns in Chicago, he can't imagine a better way to commute. He's getting exercise, drifting through fresh air and catching glimpses of neighborhood life — a recently opened coffee shop or a diving owl at night —that he's convinced he'd miss if he were driving.

If you’ve considered bike commuting but assumed you needed expensive gear and to be in excellent physical shape, or worried about arriving at work disheveled or smelly, there are ways to overcome those hurdles. Cycling can be a healthy, enjoyable and affordable way to a job site, especially at a time of elevated gasoline prices.

“It’s such a great, practical invention that I became enamored with as a little kid, and I find it just as valuable as a 72-year-old,” Roper, owner of the Hopleaf Bar and restaurant, said.

Below, experienced cyclists and bike safety advocates share tips on how to get started and arrive safely at your destination while still looking reasonably workplace-presentable.

You don't have to buy fancy equipment to commute by bike

Some cyclists splash out on pricey gear such as foldable bikes, premium padded shorts and waterproof bags. Specialty cycling equipment can be fun, but you can spend less and still have a great ride. If you don't want to purchase a bicycle, consider a bike-sharing program that rents two-wheelers for short rides.

Natalie Frank, 22, didn't have extra cash when she graduated from college and landed a job as a software engineer in the Boston office of technology company Topsort. She asked her friends if anyone had a bicycle they no longer wanted, and a free road bike was hers a few weeks later.

If the tires need air, she fills them using free pumps located in city parks.

“My commute costs zero dollars. That’s crazy,” Frank said.

Wash up and switch outfits to look presentable after a ride

Many cyclists reach their workplaces a few minutes early to freshen up and change into work clothes. Some bike commuters leave a spare set at their desks. Like many others, Frank carries clothing in a backpack along with her laptop.

Ellie Dannenberg, 37, a University of Denver math professor, commutes in gym clothes and carries a work outfit in panniers, which are storage bags and baskets that attach to a bicycle. She stashes a pair of work shoes in her office.

“Investing in pannier bags is a really great thing to do, especially for the commute to work when you probably don’t want to show up super sweaty,” Dannenberg said. “Backpacks are heavy, they’re more uncomfortable, and then you end up with a sweaty back when you get there.”

On Denver's wetter days, Dannenberg wears rain pants and a waterproof jacket that fits over her helmet.

Some office buildings have showers for washing up, but many don't. Keeping body wipes, rinse-free cleanser or deodorant at work can help you feel polished.

Use helmets and positioning to protect yourself on roads

Cyclists and safety advocates strongly recommend wearing a helmet to protect your head in case of a crash. Wearing bright colors or reflective vests and attaching lights and reflectors to the bicycle improves visibility.

Roper wears a yellow-green helmet and has front and rear lights that flash. “You really can't fail to see me,” he said.

To ensure you’re seen when traveling on smaller roads without bike lanes, ride in the middle of the lane, and if you’re at a stop light, go to the front of the traffic, Dannenberg suggested.

Watch out for black ice in the winter. “If you’re running late and there’s ice on the road, it’s worth it to slow down around the corners,” Dannenberg added.

The League of American Bicyclists has videos on its website covering traffic safety and hand signals, which cyclists can use to communicate when they’re turning or stopping.

New riders may want to find a biking companion who can point out safer, less congested routes.

“It’s nice to have a buddy if you know someone who’s commuting by bike in the vicinity that you’re going,” said Alison Dewey, education director at The League of American Bicyclists. “Maybe the most enjoyable route is just going another half-mile in this direction and getting on a trail instead of a more direct way. Someone who’s more experienced might know that.”

Some riders prefer electric bikes with a pedal-assist feature that provides a boost when they want to keep pace with traffic. After stopping at intersections, e-bikes help cyclists get going again, Dewey said.

Watch out for obstacles and swinging car doors to stay safe

When riding next to parked cars, leave space between yourself and those vehicles so you don't get “doored” — a common cycling collision that happens when someone opens a car door in a moving rider's path.

The League of American Bicyclists recommends staying four feet away from parked cars, even if it means positioning yourself outside of a marked bike lane. “It’s more important to be out of the ‘door zone’ than to be in the bike lane,” Dewey said.

Scan parked cars to see if anyone's inside, and if you notice a driver or passenger, move over, because you don't want to be next to that door when it opens, Dewey said.

If you do get into a crash with a car, call the police, gather information to identify the driver and don't hesitate to get medical treatment, advised Daniel Flanzig, a lawyer who is board president of the New York Bicycling Coalition, a nonprofit which advocates for bicycle-friendly policies.

“Be vigilant when you’re riding,” he said. “Things can come at you as a cyclist. Whether it’s a car or a pothole or a road defect, there’s a lot of hazards out there that we have to keep our head on the swivel for.”

Savor the exhilaration of riding outside

Starting the day with outdoor exercise helps many riders show up to work refreshed and energized.

“Biking is genuinely probably one of the best parts of my day. I get to listen to music. I get to be by myself. I get to think,” Frank said. “Biking feels like it’s reclaiming some of the autonomy of my day, like the joy and whimsy of moving around, especially in the city."

Dewey, 52, enjoys views of the Potomac River as she pedals 16 miles to work.

“It brings me a lot of happiness to just ride,” Dewey said. “Being outside is just always good for my emotional health. And honestly, I like being under my own power.”

Google has been fined 890 million euros (£759 million) by the EU for breaching its laws including by giving more prominence to its own services such as shopping, hotels and sports scores in search results.

The European Commission, which is the EU’s executive arm and enforces competition rules, handed out two separate fines worth 460 million euros (£392 million) and 430 million euros (£367 million).

It said it found two cases of non-compliance, one for self-preferencing on Google Search, and another for preventing the steering of customers towards potentially cheaper services on Google Play.

Google breached the Digital Markets Act by giving preferential treatment to its own services, including shopping, hotels, sports results and transport, over those of other firms in Google Search, according to the commission.

It did this by displaying them more prominently in search results, such as by bumping them up to the top of the page or by using enhanced visuals and filters, which others do not get.

The commission also found that Google prevented app developers from offering cheaper offers to customers in the Google Play app store.

The fine marks the latest big crackdown from the Brussels-based commission which has been taking enforcement action across the big tech industry.

Google recently lost its appeal against a 4.1 billion euro (£3.5 billion) fine imposed by the EU for limiting competition and reducing consumer choice through the dominance of its mobile Android operating system.

Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission’s executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, said: “Google must now bring the non-compliance to an end and to refrain from continuing it in the future.

“Today’s decisions send a clear message: we will not hesitate to use our tools to safeguard business and innovation opportunities opened up by the Digital Markets Act.”

Google has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

After missing out on Victor Munoz and Johan Manzambi, Newcastle United are closing in on a fourth signing of the summer. The Magpies are on the verge of signing Aladji Bamba from Monaco with the 20-year-old flying to the North East to complete his move.

Liverpool are facing a crucial summer under new head coach Andoni Iraola and amid the backdrop of takeover talks, the former Cherries boss wants transfers.

The Reds made an approach for PSG target Maghnes Akliouche with the Parisiens unable to meet the demands of Ligue 1 rivals AS Monaco. Meanwhile, Liverpool are said to be leading the race to sign Bradley Barcola, a move which would be another blow for Arsenal, who are also rumoured to hold an interest.

There's a month to go until the Premier League returns, and with pre-season getting underway across the division, the transfer action is picking up. Chelsea completed a deal to sign England star Morgan Rogers after footing up a £117million fee to set the pace for the summer.

Arsenal are set to welcome Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, but their bid to sign Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes is stealing the headlines. The Magpies remain adamant that their captain is not for sale but could they see an Alexander Isak repeat?

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed
Sports.content:
Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed

The Spain captain is on a high after winning the World Cup and being named player of the tournament, but his club future has been in question for some time

View 2 Images Rodri of Manchester City (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Manchester City bosses will resist all attempts from Real Madrid to sign Rodri this summer.

‌



Spanish giants Real have made the World Cup winner one of their No.1 priorities. Rodri has entered the final 12 months of his current deal and has not agreed a new one at the Etihad.

‌



The midfielder's stock has never been higher, following his sensational exploits with Spain in North America this summer and one particular high-profile social media account has gone into overdrive in recent days.

‌



Real president Florentino Perez is said to be preparing an initial £80m bid - and is even prepared to go to £100m for someone who will be available on a free transfer in 12 months time. But City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak is set to hold firm - and rebuff his rivals from the Spanish capital.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola names his price after job rejection as England possibility opens up READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

New boss Enzo Maresca has made it clear he wants to keep Rodri at all costs.

‌



Maresca, who will speak to the media for the first time on Friday since replacing Pep Guardiola, made this stipulation when negotiating his deal to become the new manager six months ago.

The Italian is planning to build his team around Rodri, and views the defensive midfielder as crucial when it comes to integrating new £116m signing Elliot Anderson into the side.

View 2 Images Rodri helped Spain to the World Cup this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



City bosses are still hopeful of agreeing a new deal with Rodri that would secure his long-term future. But despite all his success in Manchester, the 30-year-old still harbours long-held ambitions to play for Real before he retires.

Which means he could decide to run down his contract and leave the Etihad for nothing next summer.

Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019 for £62.6m and has gone on to become one of the most decorated players in the club's history.

‌



Rodri has won 13 major trophies, including the Treble in 2023, as well as winning the Ballon d'Or in 2024, at the expense of Real's Vinicius Junior.

He is also favourite to land the individual honour again next time round.

Sports.title: Man City had more fans arrested than any other club in 2025-26 as top five revealed
Sports.content:
Man City had more fans arrested than any other club in 2025-26 as top five revealed

Data has been released surrounding football-related arrests during the 2025-26 season and Manchester City fans topped the table ahead of Chelsea

View 2 Images There were 1,963 football related arrests last season (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City supporters were arrested the most out of all football fans last season, new police figures have revealed. The UK Government released data looking at the 2025/26 campaign.

‌



The data, which accounts for data collected by the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales, and by the British Transport Police (BTP), has taken a close look at the amount of football-related arrests and action taken by the authorities over the past 12 months.

‌



In all, it has confirmed that there were 1,963 football-related arrests and other police actions across the country. This is actually a decrease of 4% compared to last season.

‌



This is a noteworthy figure given the change in legislation midway through the season. In March, it was confirmed that unauthorised entry to a football stadium was added to Schedule 1 of the Football Spectators Act 1989. In all, 45 arrests and police actions were made for offences of that nature.

Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules READ MORE :

When it comes to specific clubs, the Government have confirmed that Man City had the most arrests, closely followed by Premier League rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The data read: “The club with the highest number of supporters arrested or subject to other police actions in the 2025 to 2026 domestic football season was Manchester City, with 102 arrests and other police actions. Chelsea was second, with 76, and Manchester United third, with 67.”

‌



Other clubs to feature in the top five include Premier League champions Arsenal, who had 66 arrests, while Championship side Millwall are slightly behind with 63.

View 2 Images Man City fans had the most arrests last season according to Government data (Image: Getty Images)

The data added: “In the 2025 to 2026 domestic football season, Manchester United had the largest decrease in the number of supporters arrested or subject to other police actions compared with the 2024 to 2025 season (-60; -47%). This follows a large increase in the number of arrests and other police actions in the 2024 to 2025 season (+39; +44% compared with the 2023 to 2024 season).”

‌



“Portsmouth had the largest increase in arrests and other police actions compared with the 2024 to 2025 season (from 16 to 55 arrests and other police actions).”

A number of high-profile Premier League clubs also feature in the list of the highest amount of football banning orders. West Ham remain at the top of the list with 121, compared to 112 last season. Chelsea, Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool also rank in the top five, with each of those clubs having supporters in the 80s with football banning orders.

Sports.title: FIFA announce World Cup team of the tournament as baffled fans say 'what a joke'
Sports.content:
FIFA announce World Cup team of the tournament as baffled fans say 'what a joke'

The World Cup team of the tournament that FIFA revealed has left fans baffled because there are some players who can count themselves unfortunate not to feature

View 2 Images Fans online are fuming about the lack of Spain players in FIFA's Dream XI (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA's fan-voted World Cup dream XI does not feature Golden Glove winner Unai Simon or Young Player Award recipient Pau Cubarsi. Vozinha is in goal with almost 40% of the votes, while Dayot Upemecano and Lisandro Martinez are the two central defenders chosen by fans.

‌



Of those two, the France international received the most votes, with nearly 15%, while his defensive partner in this team barely managed 10%. The two full-backs selected are Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, both of Spain.

‌



Real Madrid's new left-back won 23% of the vote. His international team-mate is on the right with approaching 19%.

‌



Lots of fans online have been left happy that Spain's goalkeeper and teenage defender are not included, though. In response to a FIFA social media post announcing the team, many expressed their feelings.

Pep Guardiola names his price after job rejection as England possibility opens up READ MORE :

One said: "Golden glove winner is not the GK of the tournament. What a joke." Another added: "Why is there no Cubarsi in the defence?"

A further user replied on X: "This should be a prank, right? Where's Cubarsi? Where's Simon, who collected the Golden Glove?" One more asked: "Martinez over Cubarsi? Are we for real… him, Laporte and Unai kept it only one goal all World Cup."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

There were, though, fewer complaints about the rest of the team. England star Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rodri make up the midfield three.

However, despite receiving the Golden Ball, Spain's captain has just 15% of the vote. That total is some way behind Bronze Boot winner Bellingham's 29% and Olise's 19%.

‌



Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi are the front three. This summer's Golden Boot and Bronze Ball winner leads the way with almost 30% of the vote, with Haaland on 27% and Messi at 22%, despite having a Silver Ball and Silver Boot to go along with his runners-up medal.

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham is the only England player to be included in the XI

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The vote was open for 48 hours after the World Cup final. There were also votes for the standout players - one goalkeeper, one defender, one midfielder and one forward - after every round throughout the tournament to build a shortlist.

The four winners from each round made the shortlist. They joined "additional players identified by FIFA based on their performances during the tournament". Cubarsi was not the top-voted defender after any of the seven rounds.

Simon did make it with almost 45% of the goalkeeper vote after the semi-finals. Vozinha, however, averaged 50% when winning round one and the round of 32.

Sports.title: Mateus Fernandes shows Man Utd what they're missing with screamer on Spurs debut
Sports.content:
Mateus Fernandes shows Man Utd what they're missing with screamer on Spurs debut

Mateus Fernandes was linked to Manchester United this summer but the former West Ham man opted for a move to Spurs instead and has kicked off his career in North London in style

View 2 Images Mateus Fernandes scored a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut (Image: Sky Sports)

Mateus Fernandes has enjoyed a blockbuster start to his Tottenham career with a stunning goal on his debut. The Portuguese midfielder completed a move to North London last month in an £85million switch from relegated West Ham.

‌



Fernandes, 22, was also linked with a switch to Manchester United but the Red Devils were unwilling to pay the amount that the Hammers demanded for his services.

‌



Instead, they have paid a combined £85m for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively. And while United will reflect positively on their own business, they might have some slight regret if Fernandes’ pre-season strike for Spurs is anything to go by.

‌



Roberto De Zerbi’s side took on MK Dons in their pre-season opener on Wednesday, with Fernandes lashing home a stunning volley from outside of the box.

Richarlison risks wrath of teammates with reaction to Argentina losing World Cup final READ MORE :

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Speaking about his goal, the midfielder said: “It was great, no? The second I did the goal, I thought no I can’t shoot again because if I miss, they will say I am lucky.

“It’s given me confidence for the next game, for the next days. The most important thing is to play well, control the game. In the last minutes, I was so tired so I need to improve this as well but it’s very important for me to play well.

‌



“It was my favourite goal of my career. It was fantastic. It is number one by a mile, the second one was last season. I need to do this more times, to score a goal and shoot outside of the box. I know I can do it so this gives me confidence for the days ahead.”

View 2 Images Fernandes' effort flew into the top corner (Image: Sky Sports)

On how preparations for the 2026/27 season were going, Fernandes added: “The weather in England it’s so good, not too tough. I think it’s important for me to speak with the manager and with the guys. Everyone is incredible.

‌



“I’m very happy to be here. I know I’m playing for a massive club. We are playing for the top of the Premier League and the levels need to be big. We need to train hard to arrive in the games and compete with the opponents.”

Asked what he wants to achieve during his time with Spurs, Fernandes said: “As an individual, I want to do better than last season. I know I need to score more goals like today, get more assists. Be more constant on my game.

“Playing for Tottenham, maybe that pressure can be even more. I need to be better in many aspects and this is the reason I am here. I know Mr De Zerbi will improve me and the team and now it’s just us against the world.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola names his price after job rejection as England possibility opens up
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola names his price after job rejection as England possibility opens up

The former Manchester City boss has been in talks with Italy over becoming the national team manager.

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola has been out of work since leaving Man City at the end of last season. (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Pep Guardiola has reportedly turned down the opportunity to become Italy manager, in a potential boost for England. The Catalan coach had held talks with Italy over the vacant position, but it seems he won’t be taking the job.

‌



Guardiola is currently out of work after leaving Manchester City at the end of last season. His 10-year spell with the club saw them win six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League.

‌



He was one of Italy’s top targets for the role, but Gazzetta dello Sport reports that the situation is ‘difficult’ due to Guardiola’s salary demands and what the federation is willing to offer. It’s said Italy are willing to pay €10 million (£8.5m) per year, while the manager wants €20 million (£17m).

‌



Man City hit with brutal Rodri blow as star set to undergo surgery days after World Cup win READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp set to appoint TWO ex-Liverpool coaches in Germany backroom team READ MORE :

The former City and Barcelona boss is also reportedly concerned about the commitment required for the job, having promised his family he would spend more time with them. The 55-year-old is now back in Barcelona with his family following his exit from the Etihad Stadium.

Speaking earlier this week , FIGC president Giovanni Malago hinted at a financial disparity in talks with Guardiola. "There are certain financial aspects to be considered, and it's an understatement to say we'd have to grit our teeth for this,” he said in an interview with the Italian media.

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola left Man City this summer. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire.)

‌



"Some exceptions have been made, for example, exceptions that regard the name making such waves at the moment: Pep Guardiola. I don't need to sit here and explain the obvious reasons why he'd be an exception, but that is also no guarantee that this will go through."

The English FA could be watching the situation closely, with a long-term interest in Guardiola as England manager.

Thomas Tuchel is currently in post, and despite calls for his dismissal following the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, the FA is expected to stand by the German.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

There are, however, reports that a firm review of the team’s performance in the World Cup, where they eventually finished third, will be conducted when the dust settles .

England's attention now turns to Euro 2028, which they are co-hosting with Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland. The Three Lions have made it to the final in the last two European championships, but will be looking to go one step further this time around.

Article continues below

It’s previously been reported that Guardiola had a verbal agreement to become England boss following Gareth Southgate’s decision to step down. But the Catalan boss had a dramatic change of heart and decided to stay with City for a further two years.

Sports.title: Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules
Sports.content:
Norway to make formal Donald Trump complaint over 'serious' breach of World Cup rules

The scandal around the decision to overturn USA striker Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup continues, with Norway ready to take a stand against FIFA

View 2 Images FIFA are under pressure over Donald Trump’s interference in Folarin Balogun’s ban (Image: Alex Pantling/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA have been urged to admit wrongdoing over the decision to overturn Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup, with Norway set to make a formal complaint.

‌



US President Donald Trump admitted interfering in the process, which saw Balogun able to play for the United States against Belgium in the last 16, despite being sent off in their win over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the previous round.

‌



Trump praised FIFA for "reversing a great injustice", but his involvement led to accusations that world football's governing body had breached its political neutrality rules. The US President called FIFA president Gianni Infantino personally to discuss the issue - something Lise Klaveness, the president of the Norwegian Football Federation, says shouldn't have happened.

‌



Klaveness has previously complained about FIFA giving its inaugural Peace Prize award to Trump and says the Balogun incident is "so serious and so worrying". “To try to sweep this under the carpet now will not fly,” she said.

Klaveness told The Times: “When you bend a rule like this, you’re on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk. It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

“First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

‌



“We need our leader in FIFA to say that this was an error. If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behaviour and the organisation’s behaviour, and also the red line of what states’ leaders should interfere with. And that happened.”

View 2 Images Folarin Balogun's red card was overturned (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

If she receives the backing of her board, Klaveness plans to add the Balogun example to her complaint about the Peace Prize. And if everything goes ahead, it will go to FIFA's independent ethics committee to investigate any potential breaches.

‌



It has been reported that the decision to overturn Balogun's suspension was taken by the chairman of Fifa’s disciplinary committee, Mohammad al-Kamali, without consultation of the other committee members.

Infantino was forced to issue a statement explaining FIFA's process and his discussion with Trump during the fallout.

"FIFA's judicial bodies are independent," he said. "They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA Disciplinary Code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them. Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected."

Article continues below

"All I did was ask for a review. I didn't say, you have to do this," Trump explained at the time. "This man is a smart, tough man, Gianni Infantino. He's a smart, tough man, and his stock has gone through the roof because the job he has done has been great. I feel like we have to have all the best players on the field."

Sports.title: Maghnes Akliouche's transfer intention clear as Liverpool approach for star confirmed
Sports.content:
Maghnes Akliouche's transfer intention clear as Liverpool approach for star confirmed

Liverpool have made an enquiry over AS Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche, who is reportedly open to a Premier League move

View 2 Images Liverpool made an enquiry for Maghnes Akliouche. (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images)

Maghnes Akliouche is reportedly learning English and open to a Premier League move after Liverpool made a transfer enquiry. The Reds tested the water with Ligue 1 side, AS Monaco, for their star forward in an attempt to bolster their forward line.

‌



The Liverpool ECHO reported that talks were initiated with Monaco earlier in the transfer window as they scoured the winger market to establish the availability of the French international. Andoni Iraola's side face the need to replace Mohamed Salah and have drawn up a shortlist of targets which include Bradley Barcola, Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Said El Mala.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain, who appear to have beaten Liverpool to RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande, have reportedly had three bids for Akliouche knocked back, with the most recent offer understood to be in the region of £34million.

‌



Man City hit with brutal Rodri blow as star set to undergo surgery days after World Cup win READ MORE :

Wolves striker breaks silence after being BANNED from training ground as security called in READ MORE :

According to PA Sports, Akliouche is open to a Premier League move and has been learning English in recent months. Despite this, PSG remain frontrunners to secure the winger's signature but are continuing to pursue their targets.

Liverpool have already signed Victor Munoz, who will join his new teammates upon his return following Spain's World Cup campaign, but head coach Andoni Iraola made it abundantly clear that signing a winger this summer is a necessity.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The 44-year-old said: "No, I think it is difficult to say a number when the market is open. You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

"There are obvious situations where we need to sign players. A winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players, that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things."

‌



Akliouche's credentials match the calibre of player that Liverpool typically pursue in the transfer market, having played over 100 times.

View 2 Images The highly-rated Maghnes Akliouche has made 10 senior appearances for France, attracting interest from Liverpool and PSG. (Image: Photo by Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

He has registered 23 goals and 28 assists across 139 matches for Monaco, while he featured in Didier Deschamps' squad at the World Cup, bringing his tally of caps for Les Bleus to 10.

Article continues below

Liverpool's desire to recruit a winger has been widely documented in the wake of Salah's departure.

The club were prepared to spend £86m on Diomande, though the Ivorian has indicated a preference for joining PSG - a move which has not yet materialised.

Sports.title: Rowley steps down as St Helens head coach
Sports.content:
Paul Rowley has stepped down as St Helens coach with immediate effect.

Saints have endured a difficult season by their high standards as they currently hold the final play-off position in sixth place by two points - ahead of Hull KR who have a game in hand - having never missed the Super League play-offs.

Assistant coach Eamon O'Carroll will assume interim leadership of the team ahead of their Rivals Round match against Wigan Warriors on Friday, live on Sky Sports at 8pm (build-up from 7.30pm).

"I would like to thank Paul for his commitment and extreme hard work as our head coach. He will always be warmly welcomed at the club," said St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus.

"The decision was an extremely difficult one for all concerned, and we fully recognise the extra challenges that Paul faced with us this particular season.

"We as a club must now look forward and do all within our powers to preserve our position as the most successful club in the history of Super League and to restore our position as a silverware contender going forward."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between St Helens and Toulouse earlier this month

Rowley became Saints head coach at the end of last year after a troubled season with Salford Red Devils, where financial issues led them to finish bottom of the Super League.

Saints are six points behind league leaders Leeds Rhinos but suffered a 46-0 hammering to Toulouse earlier this month - the first time they had been held scoreless at home since 1980.

They were also thrashed 32-0 by Wigan Warriors in the semi-finals of the Challenge Cup.

Singh on set at Sky Sports News

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Harry Kane reflects on England's third place at the World Cup, backs head coach Thomas Tuchel to succeed with England and does not rule out playing one more World Cup.

Had things worked out differently, Singh could have been lining up alongside Kane at club level next season. Singh spent four seasons with Bayern Munich after the Bavarian giants signed him following his impressive showing for New Zealand at the 2019 FIFA U20 World Cup.

"It was such an unreal experience," said Singh, who played against Tottenham in the 2019 Audi Cup final before making his Bundesliga debut later that year.

"It was amazing to be around one of the biggest clubs in the world and to learn from some of the best on a daily basis.

"Hansi Flick (the current Barcelona manager) was in charge. Alphonso Davies and Joshua Zirkzee were there at the time, so we are all mates."

An investment consortium led by British-Indian millionaire and former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia has expressed an interest in acquiring a minority stake in Liverpool.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) acknowledged the approach on the same day that Bhatia stepped down from the board at QPR to end an 18-year association, having agreed to transfer his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

A spokesperson for FSG said: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

Sky News has since revealed that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has also been approached to join the consortium.

No deal has been agreed with discussions at an early stage. FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 for £300m. Forbes recently valued the club at £4.6bn.

On Tuesday, Bhatia announced he was leaving his role at QPR, saying the club "has been a deeply important part of my life and of my family's life". He served as vice-chairman before becoming chairman in 2018, a role he held for five years.

Image: Will Amit Bhatia succeed in his attempt to acquire a strategic minority stake in Liverpool Football Club?

Bhatia is the son-in-law of Lakshimi Mittal, who is the executive of steel and mining company ArcelorMittal.

Mittal is worth an estimated £23.2bn.

Miami Heat have confirmed a video teasing LeBron James' potential return to the NBA franchise was posted by mistake.

A live stream titled "LeBron James Introductory Press Conference", scheduled for July 27, was uploaded to the Heat's YouTube channel on Tuesday night but was later deleted.

A Miami Heat spokesperson later confirmed the video was mistakenly posted in preparation for James potentially returning to the team with which he won two championships.

The error has sent the basketball world into a frenzy as it awaits confirmation of where James will play his 24th NBA season.

James' next step has dominated the news agenda ever since the 41-year-old confirmed he would be leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons in June.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat have all been linked with the four-time NBA MVP.

Sports.title: Leeds in talks with Man City over deal for Trafford
Sports.content:
Leeds United are in talks with Manchester City over a deal for goalkeeper James Trafford.

The England international is Leeds' primary goalkeeper target.

Newcastle and Aston Villa have also had an interest this summer in Trafford, but Leeds are understood to be the most advanced in their pursuit.

The 23-year-old played 17 times for City in 2025/26, following a move back to the Etihad from Burnley, keeping eight clean sheets.

He then travelled to the 2026 World Cup with England, but did not make an appearance for Thomas Tuchel's side.

Leeds have lost goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier this summer, with the pair joining Man Utd and Arsenal respectively.

They are understood to be hopeful about their chances of signing Trafford.

Finding a new first-choice goalkeeper is a priority for Leeds this summer after Darlow's exit and an unconvincing debut season for Lucas Perri.

Perri, who was dropped by Daniel Farke last season, and third-choice Alex Cairns are the only senior goalkeepers currently on Leeds' books.

There is the potential for Perri to depart this summer amid interest from Torino.

However, Leeds are unwilling to part with the Brazilian until they have brought in at least one goalkeeper.

Sports.content:

Saliba has avoided the need for surgery after injuring his back during France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain but the 25-year-old faces a lengthy period of rehabilitation.

Stones is available as a free agent having reached the end of his contract at Manchester City last month. Sky Sports News has reported the England defender is also a target for Chelsea.

The 32-year-old worked with Mikel Arteta during the Arsenal manager's time as assistant to Pep Guardiola at City.

Image: Konsa appeared in all eight England games at the World Cup

Konsa, who represented England alongside Stones at the World Cup, is four years younger than Stones at 28 and has two years remaining on his contract at Aston Villa.

Sky Sports News understands Arsenal have been exploring the cost of a potential deal for Konsa but there is a significant gap in valuation with Villa.

Both Konsa and Stones can also operate at right-back.

Arsenal have consolidated their defensive options by completing the permanent signing of Piero Hincapie following his loan spell from Bayer Leverkusen last season.

They also have Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber and Ben White as centre-back options.

Image: Arsenal's win rate drops from 68 per cent to 50 per cent without William Saliba starting

White has returned to training following the knee injury he suffered in May, while Timber said this week he is "hopefully back soon" as he continues his rehabilitation from a groin problem.

Arteta an admirer of Stones

It's easy to see the logic behind Arsenal's interest in Stones. He is available on a free transfer and brings a wealth of experience following a glittering 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium during which he won 17 trophies including six Premier League titles.

Arteta knows his game intimately having worked with him for three years under Guardiola and confirmed his admiration when Arsenal were rumoured to be interested in signing him in 2020.

Image: Stones featured five times for England at the World Cup

"John is a player I really like," he said. "We followed him before we signed him when I was at City. I worked with him for many years. I know him well and when I look at centre-backs, he has many attributes that I like."

Stones' availability on a free adds to his appeal as someone who could provide short-term cover for Saliba having proved his fitness at the World Cup, where he made five appearances for England over the course of the tournament.

His injury history is, however, a concern.

Stones was limited to only 439 Premier League minutes last season due to thigh, calf and muscular injuries, and only played 547 minutes in another disrupted campaign before that.

The former Everton defender did not play more than 59 per cent of Premier League minutes in any of his 10 seasons at Manchester City.

Konsa attractive but tougher deal to do

Konsa offers far more robustness than Stones. He has made a minimum of 33 Premier League starts in five consecutive seasons for Aston Villa and has no history of significant injury.

Like Stones, he is comfortable in possession and able to withstand opposition pressure on the ball. He primarily plays as a right-sided centre-back, in the same position as Saliba, but showed his capacity to play at right-back during the World Cup.

Image: Konsa had the highest ground-duel success rate in the Premier League last season

Konsa also boasts outstanding physical qualities and ranks as one of the Premier League's best one-on-one defenders. In fact, according to Opta, he had the highest ground-duel success rate of any outfield player in the Premier League last term, at 73 per cent.

That combativeness is sure to appeal to Arteta but signing him over Stones would require a far greater financial outlay on a player who turns 29 in October, with Aston Villa said to value him at £60m.

Sports.title: Salt stars as Fire end eight-match Hundred losing streak against Brave
Sports.content:
Phil Salt weathered a bowling storm from England fast bowler Jofra Archer as the Welsh Fire captain led his side to a six-wicket victory over Southern Brave in The Hundred.

The win snapped Fire's eight-match losing streak against Brave, with Salt carrying the team over the line in dramatic fashion.

After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire found themselves needing 14 runs off 10 balls at the end of their innings, and Salt, alongside Asa Tribe, showed his composure to whittle down the tally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire's Phil Salt whittled down the run chase and secured victory with a six

Salt, who struck an unbeaten 47 off 37 deliveries, found himself on strike with only four runs left to win from three deliveries, and the captain swept away Chris Jordan for a big six to wrap up the victory.

"The conditions weren't easy. It was a good toss for us to win and chasing the target, we knew what it was," Salt told Sky Sports.

"We were electric in the field. There was some real good catching on display. We got off the rope well today. Bowling-wise, we put the ball in the right areas. Did we do it for long enough? Were we smart enough? That's one for the coaches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Miller (44) and Thomas Rew (41) struck the highest individual scores for the Brave

Brave started slowly, with Sam Cook first snaring Jamie Smith for three runs, before Marco Jansen had Ben McKinney for four.

Thomas Rew (41) and David Miller (44) steadied the ship, before Jansen hit back with his second of the match to dismiss the former off 30 balls.

Archer came to the crease but was run out in the most bizarre of circumstances. Miller had struck a ball to Jansen at cover, and the England seamer had attempted to get up for a single, but his batting partner sent him back, turning in a circle in the middle of the wicket as Fire made the pair pay for their miscommunication.

Salt and Matthew Short arrived at the crease after the intermission, with Short bringing up a score of 20 before being caught out at extra cover by Dan Worrall.

Worrall was back in on the action again, combining with Smith to dismiss England legend Joe Root for 15 runs.

Image: Former England captain Joe Root was dismissed for 15 runs after he was run out by Dan Worrall and Jamie Smith

Rachin Ravindra arrived at the crease, and it was here that the Fire kicked on, with he and Salt bringing up an impressive partnership of 49 runs off 27 balls.

"It's great to play a role in a partnership," Ravindra said to Sky Sports. "Communication was key out there between us. Salty played well out there. It wasn't such a free-flowing T20 wicket as we're used to seeing.

"He supported me greatly during that partnership, and it's great to see the skipper finish it off at the end.

"We're all used to seeing that free-flowing Phil Salt, aren't we? The comms were mostly just about hitting good cricket shots, trusting our positions, hitting the gaps hard and running hard, and the boundaries would come.

"Salty is such a special player but showed his maturity and leadership to keep us accountable ball after ball."

What's next?
