Pep Guardiola is reportedly set to reject Italy despite 'financial exceptions' having been made in an attempt to attract the legendary Manchester City boss.

Guardiola is currently out of work after leaving City at the end of last season following 10 incredible years in England where he won 20 trophies.

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC), meanwhile, have been searching for a new manager since Gennaro Gattuso resigned in April after the Azzurri failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup.

FIGC chief Giovanni Malago had outlined their interest in Guardiola earlier this week along with his determination to get a deal done at a time where the country's football team are experiencing some of their worst ever times on the football pitch.

But, according to Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport, the Spaniard is unlikely to take the role despite meeting with the FIGC's technical director Paolo Maldini and his adviser Leonardo in Barcelona last weekend.

The report states that although Malago highlighted how his federation were willing to break the bank for No 1 target Guardiola, the two parties remain far apart on figures.

Pep Guardiola is reportedly set to reject the opportunity to take over as Italy's new manager

Italy have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups and currently do not have a manager

It is understood that Guardiola wants a salary of €20million-a-year (£17m), but the FIGC have only offered around €10m-a-year (£8.5m).

The report adds that although Maldini and Leonardo, who previously served as PSG's sporting director, have a superb relationship with Guardiola, they returned from their meeting in Barcelona with 'little optimism'.

This was despite Guardiola - who spent two seasons in Italy during his playing days with Brescia and Roma and can speak the language - being offered a comprehensive project where he would have significant control over Italian football.

The 55-year-old is understood to be concerned about the commitment required by jumping straight back into management having promised his family that he would live in Barcelona now his time in England has come to an end.

Unless they give their blessing to the Italy role, it seems unlikely that Guardiola will accept the offer.

Speaking earlier this week about the former Man City, Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss, Malago had said: '[Financial] exceptions have been made, exceptions that for example may concern the name that is so overbearing in these hours: Pep Guardiola.

'Exceptions for obvious reasons that I am not here to explain, but it is not certain that this thing will go through.'

Former Italy boss Roberto Mancini and Azzurri legend Andrea Pirlo are also in the running for the role, although the likes of Antonio Conte may come into the mix if Guardiola does reject the opportunity.

Italy Under 21 boss Silvio Baldini was in temporary charge for the June international break, yet with a fresh cycle starting after the World Cup, they are keen to appoint a new manager as soon as possible.

Sports.title: How Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes proved in just 45 minutes that this is a whole new Tottenham this season - and why £185m duo's new team-mates could barely believe their eyes
Sports.content:
If first impressions are anything to go by, then Tottenham Hotspur should get used to controlling midfield.

Their new-look £185million pivot dictated play in their opening pre-season friendly – a 1-0 win against MK Dons on Wednesday – providing a 45-minute glimpse of what to expect from club record-breaking transfers Sandro Tonali (£100m from Newcastle) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m from West Ham).

Let’s get the balancing act out of the way. Yes, it was only a pre-season match. Yes, it was only one half of football. And yes, it was against inferior League One opposition, MK Dons.

But their desire to impose themselves immediately was encouraging. Fernandes took just three minutes to exhibit his natural ability. MK Dons goalkeeper Craig MacGillivray punched Mathys Tel’s corner clear, but Fernandes lurked outside the area and wrapped his right foot around the ball on the volley and hammered it into the top corner.

Pre-season or not, it was a top-quality finish - a sneak peek at his talent. Seeing the first manifestation of his £85m transfer fee, his new team-mates laughed in disbelief when the ball hit the back of the net. Spurs chiefs would have celebrated with a sigh of relief as he demonstrated the first sign of being a hit.

What a hit, Mateus Fernandes 💥



Watch our pre-season games live on SPURSPLAY! — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) July 22, 2026

Mateus Fernandes finds the top corner inside five minutes of his Tottenham debut

Sandro Tonali, whose fee could rise to £100million, also impressed in the pre-season friendly

Spurs changed their entire XI at half-time – as is customary at the start of pre-season – making the sample size small. Regardless, it was an extremely active debut. Everything went through Fernandes – he had 81 touches in the first half; no player had more.

Playing as a No 8, he was supported by fellow new arrival Tonali in a more deep-lying role. And for a pair playing together for the first time, they showed a surprising level of synchronisation. They both picked up on each other’s movement, finding space or covering when the other was on the ball.

If that can be developed in a week, then Spurs are on the right footing with this pair as they attempt to return to the top half after finishing 17th in consecutive seasons – avoiding relegation last term by just two points. Much like Fernandes, Tonali was busy – registering 70 touches; only his midfield partner had more.

Tonali was given the licence to run forward into the channels from his holding midfield role as Spurs tried to break down MK Dons’ disciplined, low block. The Italian is versatile; not only is he a ball-winner, but he has a big engine and an array of line-breaking passes at his disposal. It enables him to play as a six or an eight. Partnering Fernandes, however, it seems that can be relatively fluid.

Perhaps the biggest boost is that Spurs’ lavish midfield is well-rested after Italy failed to qualify for the World Cup, while Portugal overlooked Fernandes. It offers Roberto De Zerbi a full pre-season to get his ideas across to the heartbeat of the team, the anchors between defence and attack – a luxury that most managers do not have this summer.

What remains to be seen, though, is how they will handle teams that pose a greater threat. There was little forthcoming from the MK Dons attack, and they did not have much of the ball, which limited the occasions Spurs could press with intensity – a hallmark of De Zerbi’s teams.

The pair will need to step up to the increased workload, and that process should begin to take shape as the quality of opposition increases.

Tottenham will now jet Down Under, facing Auckland FC, Sydney FC and Chelsea, before returning to north London to play Getafe and Hoffenheim, with little under a month to go until the Premier League opener at Brentford on August 22.

Fernandes and Tonali are among £240m worth of reinforcements given to Roberto De Zerbi this summer

There were a couple of mistakes. Both gave the ball away in dangerous areas as MK Dons embarked on encouraging counter-attacks. Tonali was bailed out by an offside flag, Fernandes by a lung-busting run from a recovering defender. The pair deserve the benefit of the doubt for a couple of misplaced passes at the start of pre-season, though.

It was an exhibition of intelligent passes in the main – particularly from Tonali, who played a pivotal role in transition as he shifted the ball into wide areas.

His highlight came as he carried the ball from deep towards the halfway line before disguising a bending pass with his right foot into the feet of Tel, who cut inside and squared to Conor Gallagher inside the penalty area. An incisive move from back to front – crafted by Tonali – Gallagher couldn’t quite connect to top it off.

On the basis of this showing, the Englishman will need to step it up to keep up with Spurs' new dynamic duo.

Sports.title: Norway set to launch formal complaint to FIFA over Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card interference - amid fears president Gianni Infantino is trying to sweep scandal 'under the carpet'
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA are preparing to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Donald Trump's interference in Folarin Balogun's red card-ban at the World Cup.

USMNT striker Balogun was sent off during their last-32 tie against Bosnia and Herzegovina, meaning he was set to be banned from their last-16 clash against Belgium in a huge blow to Mauricio Pochettino's side.

However, Balogun's ban was suspended by FIFA after a phone call from Trump to Gianni Infantino, a close confidante of the US President, where he urged the football supremo to allow the striker to play.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, including claiming things 'worked out much better' when speaking ahead of Sunday's World Cup final and saying that Infantino made a 'great decision'.

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the footballing world, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness revealed they are planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee, becoming the first national federation to formally make a stand over the issue.

In an interview with The Times, Klaveness, whose NFF body also complained about Trump being handed a FIFA Peace Prize award by Infantino last year, urged the FIFA chief, who is under fire for potentially breaching political neutrality rules, to admit his organisation made a mistake with the Balogun saga.

The Norwegian FA are planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Balogun was sent off in the last-32 stage, but Donald Trump intervened and the striker's ban was suspended so he could play in their last-16 clash against Belgium

'When you bend a rule like this, you’re on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behaviour and the organisation’s behaviour, and also the red line of what states’ leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

It was reported last week that the decision to suspend Balogun's red card was ultimately taken by Mohammad al-Kamali, the chairman of that disciplinary committee, yet the official was not said to consult any of the other 17 members of his committee.

Norwegian Football Federation President Lise Klaveness pictured with Gianni Infantino

Klaveness admitted that FIFA had a 'very powerful voice in their ear' but argued that by refusing to consult more widely, they made a 'mistake' and a 'controversial decision'.

She also highlighted that she was 'disappointed but not necessarily surprised' by FIFA's lack of transparency around the whole situation.

Klaveness added: 'To try to sweep this under the carpet now will not fly. Too many felt this… coaches, players, fans… that this was too close to the game.'

Klaveness said the case was 'so serious' and 'so worrying', revealing that she would discuss it with her board, and if they backed her position, an official complaint would be launched.

Sports.title: Wolves star breaks silence after club CANCELLED training because he refused to leave the pitch - and hired extra security to keep him away
Sports.content:
Wolves star breaks silence after club CANCELLED training because he refused to leave the pitch - and hired extra security to keep him away

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare has hit back after reports that Wolves cancelled training on Monday because of his behaviour.

The 25-year-old says he has upheld the 'highest training standards' despite the controversy that has rocked Wolves' pre-season.

On Monday, Arokodare stood his ground when new manager Cesar Peixoto told him not to train with the first team.

Wolves organised extra security at their training ground, Compton Park, to prevent the 25-year-old from entering on Tuesday.

But Arokodare has posted on Instagram: 'Throughout my career, I have always taken great pride in conducting myself professionally and maintaining the highest professional standards.

'My commitment has always been to prepare myself as well as possible so that I can contribute to my team-mates and the club whenever I am called upon.

'I remain under contract with Wolves, and my only intention is to fulfil my responsibilities professionally by training, doing my job, and contributing to the team in accordance with that contract.'

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare has hit back after the club cancelled training because he refused to leave the pitch

New manager Cesar Peixoto initially left Arokodare out of the team's pre-season training camp

On Wednesday evening, he was unable to contribute as Wolves travelled to Maidenhead for a pre-season friendly without him, winning 1-0.

Arokodare, who spent last season with Wolves as they were relegated from the Premier League, faced disciplinary action in April after getting into a physical altercation with team-mate Mateus Mane following their 4-0 thrashing by West Ham.

He did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

Peixoto, who joined from Portuguese club Gil Vicente in June, has insisted he will be a firm hand with his players.

In his first interview, he said: 'Firstly, I'm a very demanding coach.

'But, I believe in giving others maximum freedom and maximum responsibility. I want us to work as a team and as a unit and build a good environment. This is important to me, but I know very well what I want from the team. I want my team to be organised with and without the ball.

'Secondly, I want a team with intensity and to be aggressive and win duels.

'The third one is I want to show the quality of the players. To play an offensive game and to try and press high. To try and be the main character of the games. I want to win games, but I want to win while playing good football. With passion and energy.

'[The supporters can expect] a team with ambition. A strong character and identity and a strong idea of the game. A team that never gives up to win three points and to try and make the fans proud.'

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry. The Nigerian striker scored three Premier League goals last campaign.

The Daily Mail Sport has contacted Wolves as well as Arokodare's representatives.

Demoting players from the first-team or forcing them to train in isolation is banned under new rules introduced by FIFA in June.

The striker faced disciplinary action after clashing with team-mate Mateus Mane - but the duo shared supportive posts in an attempt to defuse the situation

Arokodare scored three Premier League goals campaign and could be moving to Serie A

FIFA reached an agreement with FIFPRO, the worldwide players' union, to better protect players from what is deemed an 'abusive practice'.

Chelsea's 'bomb squad' and treatment of players such as Raheem Sterling has come under scrutiny in recent seasons.

Clubs could face financial or sporting punishments under the new protections unless there is a genuine sporting reason for the player's exclusion.

Banishing them from first-team training cannot now be used as a tactic just to force them to find another club.

The Daily Mail Sport has also contacted FIFA and FIFPRO.

Sports.title: Argentina assistant coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' in ugly post-World Cup final scenes - as he insists 'it was more of a push'
Sports.content:
Argentina assistant coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' in ugly post-World Cup final scenes - as he insists 'it was more of a push'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala has attempted to downplay his post-match clashes with Spain's players after the World Cup final.

Lionel Scaloni's side were so close to retaining their title on Sunday after lifting the trophy in 2022, but were beaten 1-0 by Spain following a tense and scrappy affair.

They were aggressive throughout the match, as they had been during their semi-final victory over England, yet things escalated at the end of the game.

Having already had Enzo Fernandez sent off for a wild late challenge on Pau Cubarsi towards the end of normal time, Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground by putting his hand in the Spaniard's face.

Nahuel Molina also thumped Rodri in the torso as he was running by to celebrate Spain's triumph, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Paredes even appeared to throw punches during the altercations and Ayala, who is Scaloni's assistant, held Garcia around the throat before he was caught on camera striking Dani Olmo.

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala has tried to downplay his clashes with Spain's players

Ayala clashed with Eric Garcia before he appeared to strike Dani Olmo after Sunday's final

Then, as the Spanish squad lifted the trophy, Argentina's players faced away from their opponents in what was viewed by many as a poor show of sportsmanship.

FIFA have since launched an investigation into their behaviour, which could have serious consequences for those involved.

However, Ayala has attempted to defend what happened, insisting his clash was 'more of a push than anything else'.

Addressing the incident for the first time, he told Esports Migdia on Valencia Capital Radio: 'Obviously I’m sorry. Because of my position, I can’t allow a feeling, or what I might receive from the other party, to change my mood and my actions.

'I’m sorry, but for me, these are things that stay there and that’s it. For me, things need to be put behind us and left there.

'It was more of a push than anything else, it wasn’t a punch like they’re saying, and that’s it. It was a reaction to something he said, but that’s it. If I see him, I’ll obviously apologise to him in person.'

Ayala then tried to add further context to the general ugly scenes on the pitch at the MetLife Stadium as he added: 'It’s a shame, and you have to accept the facts and the things you’ve done on the field.

'When the game ends, what I see is a fight in the middle of the pitch, and we rush to go after our players, and it ends up like that because that’s not who we are.

'I take responsibility for what I did. My intention was to go and separate them, that was my intention, but sometimes things happen and emotions run high, but that’s no excuse.

'And given my position, my behaviour has to be different, regardless of what I receive.'

Ayala (right), a former Argentine international, serves as assistant to boss Lionel Scaloni

Announcing their probe into what had gone on in the aftermath of Sunday's game, FIFA said: 'Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

'Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.'

Despite the nasty scenes, Spain midfielder Gavi, who was pushed to the ground by Paredes amid the chaos, surprisingly defended his Argentine counterparts.

During Spain's celebrations back home, Gavi was asked for his take on what had gone on and said: 'No, to tell you the truth, I don't think he (Leandro Paredes) should be suspended.

'I understand it's not a good image for children, but I think there's also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

'The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that's it. In the end, I think it's all football, and it has to be that way.'

Sports.title: National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public
Sports.content:
National Racehorse Week coming to Liverpool and Portsmouth with 76 yards open to public

Ollie Murphy, Joe Tizzard, Rebecca Menzies and Tim Vaughan will open their stables for the ten day nationwide event from August 22 to 31

View 2 Images Sam Quek and Chris Hughes in Chester during National Racehorse Week (Image: PA)

National Racehorse Week is set to return for the sixth year running and bookings are now open for this year’s ten-day programme.

‌



The nationwide event that will take place from August 22-31 will see a variety of training yards, studs and aftercare centres opening their doors to the public.

‌



This year 96 different racing venues across England, Scotland and Wales will be open to the public, alongside over 50 community events and three city activations held at some of England’s biggest cities and landmarks.

‌



Following the success of the racing pop-up in Chester city centre last year, three racing-themed pop-up experiences will arrive in city centres during the week, two in Liverpool and one in Portsmouth, when families who may never have visited a racecourse before have the chance to meet a racehorse.

Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback READ MORE :

Spaces are available for more than 15,500 people to attend events this year, an increase on last year's figure of 14,800 free spaces available to book. During the event there will be 111 public open days across 96 venues including 76 training yards, 11 studs and nine aftercare centres

‌



Ollie Murphy, Joe Tizzard, Rebecca Menzies and Tim Vaughan are among the trainers who will host tours of their facilities, providing the chance to see horses exercise on the gallops, and on the treadmills and walkers.

Murphy who is based in Warwickshire and is opening his doors to 2,000 guests this year, said: “National Racehorse week is a brilliant initiative that I am proud to have been a part of across the last four years.

View 2 Images Over 90 stables, studs and aftercare centres will be open to the public (Image: Cotswold Film/Louis Gill)

Article continues below

“It is an incredibly important event for our sport, and it is great to welcome newcomers, curious minds and sport lovers to learn more year in year out. With 2025 seeing around 700 people visiting us at Warren Chase, I hope to see even more faces joining us this year.”

Since its inception National Racehorse Week has delivered 65,000 free places for the public to visit studs, training yards, and retraining centres for free and put on an additional 190 community events connecting over 10,000 additional people.

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are finally expected to trade leather this year, and the latter has reignited their feud by throwing a verbal jab at his long-time rival

Anthony Joshua has offered to help train Tyson Fury to lose weight ahead of their all-British clash later this year.

Sports.title: Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback
Sports.content:
Frankie Dettori responds to cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback

The Italian rode competitively for last time in Brazil in February but has now been linked with a return with Amo Racing, for whom he is an ambassador

View Image Jockey Frankie Dettori celebrates with owner Kia Joorabchian after winning the Qipco Champion Stakes

Frankie Dettori has responded to a cheeky suggestion he could make another dramatic comeback.

‌



The Italian rode for the final time in Brazil in February after taking his farewell tour to South America. The legendary jockey had originally scheduled his retirement for Champions Day at Ascot in October 2023 only to reverse his decision to call it a day and continue his career in the US.

‌



The 55-year-old confirmed last November that his time there would come to an end at the Breeders’ Cup at Del Mar ahead of a short farewell trip to South America which ended in Rio de Janeiro.

‌



Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot READ MORE :

He has since taken on a role as ambassador for Kia Joorabchian’s Amo Racing, representing the football agent on the racecourse.

But rumours have surfaced about the future of the team’s retained jockey David Egan after he was overlooked for some of the Amo rides.

Joorabchian has made no comment while Egan addressed the speculation after riding a winner at Leicester on Wednesday night.

‌



“There’s been no quotes from anyone and I’d like to say no comment from me,” he told RacingTV.

“I’ve got no comment on the situation. I’m declared to ride a horse on Friday for Amo, plan to ride for him on Saturday and even into next week so no comment.”

Nevertheless online bookmaker Betway fed the rumour mill by speculating whether Dettori could be in line for a dramatic comeback.

‌



The firm offered odds of 4-1 that he would ride for Amo Racing in the UK before the end of 2027.

Spokesperson Lewis Knowles said: ''Frankie has certainly been the comeback king over the years, with more than one retirement U-turn, so you could never truly rule out a return to the saddle at some stage.

“His relationship with Kia Joorabchian and the Amo Racing operation as Racing Manager is seemingly going from strength to strength, and with a retained rider vacancy very much open, it's certainly not beyond the realms of possibility that we could see the great man in those famous purple silks once again.''

Dettori responded with a laughing emoji.

But a lot of the Americans want to do it at MSG; not Vegas, they want it at MSG."

Article continues below

Joshua and Fury signed contracts which contained a clause guaranteeing the fight would take place in the UK. But the fighters could yet be convinced to waive that right. "It was always going to be in the UK," added Hearn. "There was never any doubt this fight was in the UK until there were some approaches from America in terms of the revenue that could be achieved at MSG.

"Netflix are probably saying they prefer it there and these are elements that we don’t actually have any control over because we’re not really the purse strings behind the fight, Turki Al-Sheikh is. When you sign a contract, you expect that to be honoured and followed, and we’ve never done a deal with Turki where he hasn’t done that.

"I don’t think he’s trying to pull a fast one. I think he’s paying a lot of money for the fight, and he wants to make it as big a success for every stakeholder involved."

Sports.title: Aidan O’Brien in middle of ‘worst downturn in form’ since 2020, say stats gurus
Sports.content:
Aidan O’Brien in middle of ‘worst downturn in form’ since 2020, say stats gurus

With the Ballydoyle maestro set to saddle four horses in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes, he is experiencing his worst month of results

View 2 Images Aidan O'Brien: has had a difficult July (Image: Megan Ridgwell/The Jockey Club)

Aidan O’Brien is in the middle of the ‘worst downturn in form’ since 2020, the year of the Covid pandemic, say experts.

‌



This season the master trainer has won the Epsom Derby for the 12th time and topped the Royal Ascot trainer rankings which have established him nearly £2 million clear in the British Flat trainers championship.

‌



Yet the stable’s form has taken a unwelcome dip with ratings experts Timeform revealing that this July is not only his worst month on recent record, but that the current Flat season is the worst for the Ballydoyle handler since it introduced its ‘Run to Form’ metric was in 2012.

‌



Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot READ MORE :

O’Brien’s present record of just three wins from his last 48 runners tells part of the story but the data garnered by points to the worst downturn in form for the yard since the 2020 season which was impacted by Covid.

The form will concern punters ahead of Saturday’s King George VI and Queen Elizabeth II Stakes in which the stable is set to run Benvenuto Cellini, Minnie Hauk, Lambourn and Action at Ascot.

‌



At Glorious Goodwood next week O’Brien is expected to field high profile Group 1 contenders such as Scandinavia, Gstaad and Diamond Necklace.

View 2 Images Benvenuto Cellini: leading three-year-old in King George (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

Timeform’s ‘Run To Form’ metric compares a horse’s pre-race rating to the rating achieved, meaning that factors such as a horse’s consistency and trainer form can be assessed. It can be a much better gauge of a horse, trainer, or jockey than strike rate as it factors in much more than a simple result.

Article continues below

Senior Analyst Kieran Clark said: “With Aidan O’Brien’s ‘Run to Form’ percentage for the season currently at 54, it’s the lowest by at least five percent since we started publishing the figures.

“This is obviously a concern with major targets on the horizon for some of his stable stars in the next week and it’ll be interesting to see how those to have already run this month fare next time, particularly if the form of the yard has improved by then.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury offered world title shot instead of Anthony Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury offered world title shot instead of Anthony Joshua fight

Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua later this year in a mouthwatering all-British showdown, but WBC supremo Mauricio Sulaiman could throw a spanner in the works

View Image Tyson Fury challenges Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty)

Tyson Fury has been offered the chance to compete for a world title INSTEAD of a monumental showcase with Anthony Joshua.

‌



The 'Gypsy King' is due to return to action on Friday night against heavyweight veteran Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand. 46-year-old Wach was last seen back in March when he suffered a points defeat to Viktor Vykhryst.

‌



Fury is expected to make easy work of the Polish scrapper before facing Joshua in November - with an official date or venue yet to be confirmed. 'AJ' himself also fights this week when he faces Kristian Prenga over in Saudi Arabia a day after his rival's outing over in Thailand.

‌



But WBC supremo Mauricio Sulaiman has thrown a real spanner in the works by offering to book a fight between Fury and champion Agit Kabayel before the end of the year - in what would serve as a major blow to Joshua. When asked if the Morecambe brawler would fight for the WBC title again, Sulaiman told Betway: "He's my friend. He's my dear friend. He was our champion for several years, a very proud WBC man, family man.

"We share values, we share special moments, and we speak often. So I'm very happy to hear that he's looking great. That video he sent ahead of England vs Mexico, he looked happy. He's just a unique individual. Kayabel vs Fury, that's a very doable fight, of course.

‌



"Tyson Fury has been one of the greatest ambassadors, one of the proudest champions. I have a great respect for him and his family and his team.We had a great run for many years as our champion. Way, way back in 2011 or 2012, he was promoted by Mick Hennessy, and he had some sort of outburst, and my father had an exchange with him, and he apologised. Our relationship with Tyson Fury has lasted so long."

He added: "Maybe he doesn't even remember that. Then he wins, he beats Wladimir Klitschko, and falls into the deepest, darkest place that any human being can imagine. Then he comes out of it and becomes WBC champion.

"He's a hero for me, and I wish him well. I wish him the best always, and if he ever fights for the WBC title again, I will be there for sure. If he ever wins the WBC title again, I will be the proudest man to put the belt on Tyson Fury. He's a sensational representative of the WBC, and I love the man."

‌



FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Tyson Fury pulls rabbit out of the hat to justify Mariusz Wach fight READ MORE :

That said, Fury may not be interested after tearing into the state of the heavyweight division, including Kabayel. "All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

Article continues below

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury pulls rabbit out of the hat to justify Mariusz Wach fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury pulls rabbit out of the hat to justify Mariusz Wach fight

Tyson Fury takes on Mariusz Wach on Friday night in a warm-up fight nobody asked for - but the giant heavyweight has a trick up his sleeve

View Image Tyson Fury and Mariusz Wach face off

Tyson Fury has turned the fight nobody wanted to see into the hottest ticket in town - by competing for free.

‌



Fury had insisted he would only return to the ring to face bitter rival Anthony Joshua. But he is now putting that mega-fight at risk by taking on veteran heavyweight Mariusz Wach in Thailand tomorrow night. Fury has been criticised for his choice of opponent - but claims he won't take a penny from the clash.

‌



Instead the £250,000 banked from the 1,500 fans in attendance will be donated to a local children's charity. And Fury said: "This is a beautiful place with beautiful people and great training facilities. "I feel at peace with everything here whereas before I had a lot of pressure on me and I felt a little bit s****y all the time.

‌



"The rain at home wasn't good. I thrive in warmer climates and I feel rejuvenated. I found the Father Ray Foundation and arranged to visit. They've helped thousands and thousands of sick and deprived children all over the country. Most of their donations come from people gift-giving, rather than government funding so it means a lot to me to be able to give back.

‌



"Being a father of seven children myself, it was heartbreaking to see those little kids and to do something good for them and give back is an unbelievable opportunity for me. Which other world champion or high-level athlete on earth would do a performance in a 1,500-seater in Pattaya?

"Do you think David Beckham would play a professional football match here, or someone famous like that? They're just not going to do it, because a lot of celebrities and big sports stars think they're bigger than they actually are whereas I just think I'm the same I've always been, a big fat f***er in the shower."

Fury, who laboured to a points victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov in April, should swat Wach aside with ease. The 46-year-old has lost seven of his last 10 fights and recently switched to MMA. Earlier this year he took on three social media influencers in a ridiculous three-on-one circus fight.

Article continues below

Victory for Fury coupled with the same result for Joshua will leave the rivals free to finally face each other later this year. But Fury insists he is not looking past Wach. "Everyone comes to try and beat me up and they very rarely do," he added. "Mariusz had had a lot of professional fights and he's a big, dangerous guy.

"I've got to be on my A-game, and I've picked him because I want some good rounds out of him. He is the same size as me, the same weight as me and he's had the same amount of fights as me. He's been in there with the elite-level champions of two generations.

"I'm not interested in what's going on with Joshua. “This is about me and Mariusz, not about anybody else. I've never been one to fall into that trap, I've always taken my opponents seriously."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
