World.title: Dinamo Draw at the Start of Champions League Qualifying
World.content:
Dinamo Zagreb played out a 1-1 draw against Thun in Switzerland in the first leg of the Champions League second qualifying round. The hosts took the lead through a Brighton Labeau goal in the 20th minute, before Miha Zajc set the final score in the 86th minute. The tie will be decided in the return leg in Zagreb in a week.

Thun are the first of three potential opponents Dinamo must overcome to secure a place in the Champions League group stage. The second round is followed by the third round and then the play-off. Dinamo’s possible third-round opponent will be the winner of the tie between KÍ Klaksvík of the Faroe Islands and Lithuania’s Kauno Žalgiris. Should they fall to Thun, Dinamo would continue their European campaign in the Europa League third qualifying round against the loser of the tie between Hapoel Be’er Sheva and Vikingur.

After a quiet start, the Swiss side took the lead in the 20th minute. Fabio Fehr’s cross from the right caught goalkeeper Ivan Filipović out, and Brighton Labeau headed home to make it 1-0. Just a minute earlier, Filipović had misjudged a free-kick delivery but redeemed himself by saving two efforts from the home side.

Dinamo almost leveled quickly, but Dion Drena Beljo’s effort in the 22nd minute went straight into the hands of goalkeeper Niklas Steffen. The Thun keeper also did well to save a fine long-range attempt from Moris Valinčić in the 28th minute. Thun’s best chance to extend their lead came in the 30th minute, when Furkan Dursun found himself unmarked five metres out but headed wide of the post.

Dinamo created a few more openings before halftime, but efforts from Miha Zajc and Gabriel Vidović fell short, and Thun led 1-0.

Dinamo continued to press after the restart. In the 53rd minute, Beljo’s header from a corner was cleared off the line by a home defender, and in the 65th minute a Mislav Oršić effort was again blocked on its way towards goal. Thun threatened on the counter, coming closest in the 73rd minute when Valmir Matoshi’s shot went narrowly wide.

Dinamo’s persistence paid off in the 86th minute. Fran Topić, on since the 79th minute, supplied the assist from the right for Miha Zajc, and the Slovenian midfielder finished first-time from 17 meters to make it 1-1. The score remained unchanged until the final whistle, leaving the tie to be settled in Zagreb.

World.title: Will Smith Visits Rimac Campus Near Zagreb
World.content:
July the 22nd, 2026 – Hollywood star Will Smith paid a visit to Rimac Campus near Zagreb this week, where he was treated to something special indeed.

The well known actor was given a behind-the-scenes look at one of Croatia’s most celebrated technology companies, and judging by his reaction, he was thoroughly impressed! Poslovni reports that the Oscar-winning actor toured the state-of-the-art headquarters of Rimac Technology, meeting founder and CEO Mate Rimac while exploring the cutting-edge engineering and production facilities that have helped place Croatia firmly on the global automotive map.

During the visit, Smith experienced several of Rimac’s innovations firsthand, including the company’s world-renowned electric hypercars. Videos shared from the visit captured the actor reacting with visible excitement, laughing, shouting in amazement and expressing disbelief at the performance and technology on display. According to those present, Smith was particularly impressed by the speed, engineering and innovation that have become synonymous with the Rimac name.

putting croatian innovation on stage

Founded by Mate Rimac back in 2009, the company has grown from a small garage startup into one of the world’s leading developers of high-performance electric vehicle technology. Today, Rimac supplies advanced battery systems, electric powertrains and software to some of the biggest names in the automotive industry, while its Nevera hypercar has repeatedly broken global performance records. The Rimac Campus, located in Kerestinec on the outskirts of Zagreb, has become a symbol of Croatia’s growing reputation as a centre for advanced engineering and innovation.

Smith’s visit shines another international spotlight on one of Croatia’s biggest business success stories. Over the past few years, the company has welcomed politicians, investors, automotive executives and celebrities eager to see firsthand how a Croatian startup evolved into a global technology powerhouse. The visit also serves as another reminder that Croatia’s international reputation is increasingly being shaped not only by tourism, but also by world-class innovation and high-tech manufacturing.

more than just fast cars…

While Rimac’s electric hypercars often capture the headlines, the company has become equally important as a technology partner for the wider automotive industry. Its expertise in battery systems, electric drivetrains and vehicle software is helping shape the next generation of electric mobility, with technologies developed in Croatia finding their way into vehicles produced around the world. For Will Smith, the visit offered a glimpse into the future of transportation. For Croatia, it was another high-profile endorsement of a company that continues to demonstrate the country’s ability to compete at the highest possible levels of global technology.

World.title: Largest Croatian Cave System Was Discovered by Chance
World.content:
July the 22nd, 2026 – The largest Croatian cave system was discovered entirely by chance, and it revealed fascinating evidence of a 20,000 year old hunter…

The largest Croatian cave, located in beautiful Ogulin, is widely considered to be the country’s most remarkable archaeological and natural treasure. More interestingly still, it owes its entire discovery to pure chance.

The Đula-Medvedica Cave System, the largest cave complex in all of Croatia, was uncovered unexpectedly during railway construction back during the early 20th century. Putni kofer writes that what initially began as an ambitious but otherwise normal engineering project soon turned into one of the country’s most significant archaeological discoveries in history, revealing evidence of human life dating back tens of thousands of years.

the best discoveries usually happen by accident…

What eventually turned out to be the largest Croatian cave system ever discovered came to light while workers were building the railway through Ogulin, exposing a vast underground network hidden deep beneath the landscape. Subsequent exploration revealed kilometres upon kilometres of interconnected passages, underground chambers and various waterways, making it the largest known cave complex in Croatia and an important site for both speleologists and scientists.

a present-day window into prehistoric croatia

Among the cave’s most extraordinary discoveries was the bone of a prehistoric hunter estimated to be around 20,000 years old. Archaeologists also uncovered numerous traces of Ice Age human activity, confirming that the cave provided shelter to people living in the region during the last Ice Age. The finds have helped researchers better understand how prehistoric communities survived in what is now Croatia during one of Europe’s harshest climatic periods.

Beyond its archaeological importance, the deep Đula-Medvedica Cave System is renowned for its geological features. The labyrinth of passages includes underground rivers, enormous chambers, dramatic rock formations and unique ecosystems that support species specially adapted to life in complete darkness. Because of its scientific value and fragile environment, much of the cave remains protected and is accessible only to researchers and experienced cavers.

ogulin’s subterranean attraction

While many visitors know Ogulin as the hometown of Croatian fairy-tale writer Ivana Brlić-Mažuranić, this picturesque but often bypassed area is also home to one of Croatia’s most fascinating karst landscapes. The rich cave system lies beneath a region shaped by many sinking rivers and limestone formations that have been carved over millions of years, creating an extraordinary underground world hidden in depths, far beneath the town.

the discovery was a turning point for croatian archaeology

Over a century has now passed since its accidental discovery, and yet the Đula-Medvedica Cave System continues to provide valuable insights into Croatia’s natural and human history. From prehistoric hunter-gatherer human remains to utterly spectacular geological formations, this incredible cave stands as an eternal reminder that some of the country’s greatest discoveries have happened entirely by accident, lying patiently in wait, deep beneath the surface, until the right moment revealed them to the world.

World.title: Critics claim anti-Russian messaging in Estonian meat producer's new advert
World.content:
Rannarootsi is facing criticism over an ad some say evokes the Russia-Ukraine war and uses derogatory slang for Russian-speakers — claims the Estonian meat producer denies.

The ad, posted on social media by Rannarootsi on Tuesday, shows two men in black shirts with Ukrainian flags on them, grilling meat on a beach as plumes of smoke rise into the sky in the distance behind them.

The slogan, promoting the brand's new barbecue pork with caramelized onions, reads: "The right grill will turn a bitter onion sweet." ("Õige grill muudab kibeda sibula magusaks.")

Critics said the combination of imagery is an inflammatory reference to the Russia-Ukraine war, while the word "sibul" is also used in Estonian as a derogatory slang reference to Estonia's Russian-speaking residents.

Kõlvart: 'Who benefits from this?'

Center Party leader Mihhail Kõlvart was among those who criticized the ad. He said businesses have the right to choose their marketing strategies, but should avoid imagery that many people may view as degrading or dehumanizing.

"Amid the current difficult geopolitical situation, with security risks higher than ever, this inevitably begs the question: who benefits from such provocations?" Kõlvart wrote, noting that an ad like this certainly won't help Ukraine.

"Who gains from adding fuel to the fire when our society is already facing too much distrust, division, pain and anger?" he added.

Rannarootsi CEO Karmo Aksel denied that the ad was meant to convey any political or hostile messages.

"It's directly connected to our product and its ingredient — caramelized onion," Aksel told ERR's Russian-language online news portal. "The slogan refers specifically to that product."

CEO denies knowing slang term

Aksel said he only learned after the ad had been published that the word sibul can have a negative meaning in certain contexts.

Rannarootsi sausages at a supermarket meat counter. Photo is illustrative, Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

"I'm more aware of that now," the CEO said, denying any ill intentions. "When we came up with that post, we had only that product in mind."

The imagery, he added, was inspired by people's newsfeeds today. "Every day, we see those plumes of smoke in the news," Aksel said.

The company also denied claims the ad targets any specific ethnic groups living in Estonia.

"The text refers to the product, while the image reflects today's media landscape," the CEO emphasized. "These were simply two things that came together. We did not intend to spark any conflict with our ad."

No plans to take it down

While Aksel acknowledged that the message was not received as intended by the company's marketing department and could have been designed differently, Rannarootsi does not plan to remove the post, even amid calls to boycott its products.

"The post has already taken on a life of its own," he said. "What would be the point of deleting it now?"

According to the company, its marketing director was unavailable for comment while on vacation.

Rannarootsi Lihatööstus is one of Estonia's largest meat producers, with facilities in Lääne County producing products including sausages, ham, bacon and barbecue meat distributed nationwide.

The company split from Maag Group last year, continuing operations as an independent company with a staff of more than 230. In the nine months since, Rannarootsi reported revenue of €38.1 million and net profit of €4.7 million.

World.title: Baltics to strengthen joint energy reserves, share emergency equipment
World.content:
The Baltic states have agreed to share and jointly procure critical reserve equipment for the electricity system to strengthen the three countries' energy security.

A joint agreement signed in Riga, Latvia, on Wednesday will allow the sharing of existing critical reserve equipment and create a cooperation framework that also includes the possibility of developing a joint regional reserve in the future.

The unified approach increases the resilience of the electricity system, improves the efficiency of resource use and reduces the impact of disruptions on consumers, a press release said.

"The Baltic states have shown that energy security can best be strengthened through cooperation. A joint crisis reserve mechanism will help ensure that, in the event of serious failures or damage, the necessary reserve equipment is available in the region and can be quickly deployed. This will make our electricity system more resilient and, if necessary, support its rapid restoration," said Minister of Energy and Environment Andres Sutt (Reform).

The declaration signed by the ministers will also allow for closer cooperation between Estonia's transmission system operator Elering and the transmission system operators of Latvia and Lithuania.

As the next step, the transmission system operators will develop a mechanism for sharing existing reserve equipment and jointly assess opportunities for creating a regional reserve to be procured together in the future.

"The changed security situation and growing threats to energy infrastructure have increased the need for solutions that enable the electricity system to be restored more quickly in the event of major disruptions," the press release said.

World.title: Poll: Isamaa's Reinsalu still top choice for PM as Perling overtakes Michal
World.content:
Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu remains Estonia's top choice for prime minister, even as Parempoolsed chair Lavly Perling moves ahead of incumbent Kristen Michal (Reform).

Reinsalu remains the most preferred candidate for prime minister, though his support fell slightly over the past month, according to a poll by the nonprofit Institute of Societal Studies and Norstat.

The monthly survey asks voters who they would prefer to see as prime minister. In the latest results, Reinsalu was the top choice of 25 percent of respondents, followed by Center Party leader Mihhail Kõlvart at 24 percent.

Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) leader Martin Helme ranked third at 16 percent, while Parempoolsed chair Lavly Perling ranked fourth with 11 percent, moving ahead of current Prime Minister and Reform Party leader Kristen Michal, who polled at 10 percent support.

Rounding out the latest figures were Social Democratic Party (SDE) chair Lauri Läänemets with 8 percent and Eesti 200 leader Kristina Kallas with 6 percent support.

Martin Helme (EKRE) and Kristen Michal (Reform) in 2021. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Support for Perling rose by 2 percentage points on month, while Reinsalu's support fell by the same amount.

Kõlvart's support solid among Center supporters

Among supporters of individual parties, the leading preferred candidates for prime minister largely matched party leadership.

Kõlvart led among Center Party supporters with 84 percent, Perling among Parempoolsed supporters with 83 percent, Reinsalu among Isamaa supporters with 77 percent and Helme among EKRE supporters with 72 percent support, while support for Michal and Läänemets among Reform and SDE backers stood at 65 and 53 percent, respectively.

The monthly preferred prime minister question was included in the July 13–20 survey of 1,000 voting-age Estonian citizens. As with party support ratings, the results exclude "don't know" responses.

World.title: Reader's question: Is it OK to go running when there's hot weather in Estonia?
World.content:
While the hottest days have come and gone in Estonia this year, without the heatwave conditions seen elsewhere in Europe, summer is still not done.

More warmer days are forecast, which makes this a timely question for those who enjoy running outdoors.

Winter running brings its own challenges, but even in Estonia, the summer months are not without their difficulties. Running in the cooler morning hours is the best practice, but how well you cope with the heat depends largely on whether you have trained your body to adapt to it, according to Tallinn University exercise physiology lecturer Karmen Reinpõld, who responded to a reader's question sent to ERR's Novaator portal.

"Running outdoors in hot weather is not bad in any way, if your body has adapted to it," Reinpõld noted. At the same time, any sudden appearance of hot weather in otherwise relatively cool Estonia can cause issues if a person has not previously conditioned themselves to run in such conditions. Overheating can occur not only due to the ambient heat and sunshine itself, but also because the muscles themselves generate a great deal of heat. "This can become dangerous for the body: When the core temperature rises too high, you start feeling unwell," she explained.

It is precisely for this reason that top athletes, such as cyclists ahead of the Tour de France, undergo specific acclimatisation training. For runners acclimating to the heat, one approach is to dress more warmly than they normally would during cooler weather, or to train indoors without cooling down. "The body then makes changes to its internal systems to adapt better and cool itself more effectively. For instance, it starts sweating sooner. That cools the body, allowing it to cope much better," Reinpõld said.

Everyone tolerates heat differently, so there is no specific temperature point beyond which people should or should not run. Conversely, some people perform noticeably worse in cooler weather, as their bodies become more sluggish. "When it gets warmer, even up to 25 degrees Celsius or more, they perform well without having to do anything special," Reinpõld added. Other people, however, begin to overheat already at temperatures of 20 degrees, and with temperatures above 30 degrees Celsius, the lecturer said, almost everyone is likely to struggle to varying extents, at least to begin with.

At the end of the day, anyone — including people from Estonia and other northerly climes — can train their body to cope with hot weather. This is particularly worthwhile for those planning to take part in the first running races of the spring. "Those who want to adapt can deliberately overdress a little, for example by wearing a thicker hat and gloves, as the head and limbs are otherwise very effective at releasing heat," Reinpõld advised. Caution is needed, however: this approach should not be used across the board or throughout an entire workout, particularly during more taxing sessions. Regular short periods of such training are preferable to fewer, longer stints, or no such training at all. Without that, the body will return to its so-called comfort zone, Reinpõld said. "How quickly or how well adaptation takes place is also highly individual. People have to listen to their own bodies," she noted. Fortunately, this is a relatively straightforward thing to do: if running feels comfortable, the body is already adapting or has adapted. In short, the expert said, it is never too late to start heat acclimatisation training, though it is never too soon either. "If we've done it three or four times a week, then after at least two weeks the signs of adaptation are already clearly visible," she noted.

One of the big running events of the year is the women-only Maijooks. This takes place in mid-May, when usually the hotter weather is still to come, though spring is a good time to get acclimated to running hot. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Drink plenty of fluids and dampen your clothes

Even after getting fully acclimated, Reinpõld said, runners should still be careful to ensure they do not overheat or lose too much fluid during a run, and they still need to take on water or other fluids. "I think the most common mistake in running is that people head out for what they think is a short run, even if it's just 30 or 40 minutes, without taking any water with them," she cautioned. In genuinely hot running conditions, dehydration develops very quickly and you would need to rehydrate even within those time-frames.

In genuinely hot weather, Reinpõld recommends running in the morning. This is preferable even to the evenings, when the heat has effectively accumulated through the day and temperatures often have not yet fallen back down again. Before heading out, runners should always wear a cap or other head covering and take enough fluids with them. Dampening your running top before the run is also an effective way to prevent overheating, and is preferable to running without a t-shirt. "Sometimes we see people taking their shirts off, but that's not sensible because the sun heats the skin more directly and cooling actually gets more difficult. A wet shirt cools the body much more effectively," Reinpõld said.

One welcome development in the cooling down department, Reinpõld noted, is the growing availability of water fountains along recreational pathways. These allow runners not only to drink but also, for example, to wet their caps or anything else. "Small things like these can make a huge difference to how good you feel when you return from a run," she added.

Pay attention to others as well as yourself

When looking out for signs of overheating or dehydration on a hot day, it is important to pay attention to other runners, as well as oneself. But how can you tell when someone has pushed themselves too hard while running on a hot day? "If we're with someone who is pushing themselves and their speech or behaviour starts becoming a little unusual, that may indicate they're overheating," Reinpõld said.

As for one's own well-being: "Often the pace is low enough and the heart rate isn't particularly high, but the body simply won't let you push any harder," Reinpõld described. "This is the first sign that overheating symptoms are approaching: weakness, thirst, dizziness, headache and nausea begin to appear." It is wiser to break into a walk instead of continuing to push yourself to run in such cases. It is vital to drink, cool yourself down and move into the shade if you continue to feel below par. "If your brain starts telling you, figuratively speaking, that it won't let you go any farther, you should definitely slow down, walk and see what happens next," Reinpõld said.

Ultimately, the most important thing while running is to trust your own feelings and judgment, including if you start getting to a stage where sound judgment faculties themselves are at risk. "If the situation gets confusing and you can't tell what's happening, it's sensible to state you should hold back," Reinpõld noted. The Tallinn Marathon and its supporting events take place in September, meaning serious entrants have to train through summer in any case.

World.title: Erki Nool and Finnish athlete Saga Vanninen end coaching cooperation
World.content:
Legendary Estonian decathlete and now coach Erki Nool and Finnish athlete Saga Vanninen have parted company. Vanninen said she wanted to train more in her home country.

The Finn took world and European indoor championship titles under the Estonian's coaching.

Nool, who took decathlon gold at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, was appointed coach to Vanninen, a combined events athlete, in November 2024,. The Finn had ended her partnership with her previous coach following an unsuccessful summer championship season.

On Tuesday, the 23-year-old Vanninen announced that she will now continue training under her compatriot Jarno Koivunen, and she will be relocating north of the Gulf of Finland, to Turku, next month.

"I am very excited. I believe I can create a home-like environment in Turku, and that is important to me. I have been travelling a lot lately, but Turku offers good training conditions and allows me to stay in one place," Vanninen said via a press release.

Erki Nool. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Vanninen praised Nool following her time training with him. "I learned a great deal under his guidance. Erki's strength is making training enjoyable. The experiences he brought with him from his own athletic career are something I could not have gained anywhere else," she said.

Nool was understanding of Vanninen's decision too. "Saga wanted to spend more time in Finland during the winter and spring. At one point she said she felt as though she was living in her car," Nool recounted.

"When [Estonian multi-event athlete] Pippi Lotta Enok, who trained together with Saga, was sidelined for six weeks through illness, Saga was training more or less on her own all the time, which she was not used to. I don't know if it's the right term, but she got homesick," Nool added.

Under Nool's guidance, Vanninen won the pentathlon in both the European indoor title and the World Athletics Indoor Championships last year. At the World Championships in Tokyo in last September, the Finn had to settle for seventh place in the heptathlon.

World.title: 30 public figures nominate piano maker Indrek Laul to run as president
World.content:
The CEO of the grand piano factory, Estonia, Indrek Laul, has been nominated as a presidential candidate by dozens of public figures ahead of this autumn's elections.

The group backing the 58-year-old includes entrepreneurs, academics, and cultural figures. This is the third time Laul has been proposed for the role.

"Estonia is at a stage where the future increasingly depends on whether we can define our shared interests and bring together knowledge, culture and entrepreneurship to achieve them," the group wrote in an open letter.

"In a rapidly changing world, we must safeguard our country's security, social cohesion and trust in democratic institutions. This requires common ground and a spirit of cooperation between different worldviews and fields of life. This is precisely the kind of balance we expect from the President of the Republic of Estonia – a person who understands Estonia's identity, can speak to and unite the people of Estonia, and represent our country with dignity and conviction around the world. We believe that Indrek Laul's life and work to date embody these competencies and values," the group's public letter of support states.

The 30 signatories include opera singers Annely Peebo and Ain Anger, conductors Kristjan Järvi, Paavo Järvi, and Hirvo Surva, poet Doris Kareva, composers Erkki-Sven Tüür and Alisson Kruusmaa, former CIO of the Estonian government Taavi Kotka, Tallink Grupp board member Piret Mürk-Dubout, and businessman Ain Hanschmidt.

Indrek Laul. Source: Kai Väärtnõu/ERR

The signatories say Laul's track record demonstrates broad-mindedness, balance, and dedication to Estonia's development.

"We are convinced that he has both the willingness and the ability to fulfill the demanding role of President of the Republic, unite the people of Estonia, and stand up wisely in times of peace and resolutely in difficult moments for Estonia's constitutional values and long-term interests. We believe that his candidacy deserves substantive, dignified and unbiased discussion both in public and in the Riigikogu. The election of Estonia's president will determine what values we wish to present to the world through the face of our country. We hope that the parliamentary parties and those participating in the presidential election will consider Indrek Laul's candidacy with an open mind and the utmost seriousness," the letter concluded.

Laul's name was floated as a possible candidate during the later stages of the 2016 presidential elections, which ultimately installed Kersti Kaljulaid as head of state.

At the last elections, in 2021, Laul himself sent a letter to the prime minister and members of the Riigikogu discussing the role of the presidency and its possibilities, which was interpreted as a sign that he was putting himself forward as a candidate, though again he never formally ran. Alar Karis was elected unopposed at the second Riigikogu ballot in August 2021.

Nomination opens on August 21

The window to officially nominate candidates is open August 21–24 inclusive, ahead of the first round of voting at the Riigikogu on September 2. Candidates are required to give their consent to run before registry and after being proposed.

Estonia's presidents are elected by the Riigikogu and not elected directly by the public. A candidate needs to win a two-thirds majority (68 votes or more in favor) to become president.

Other public figures proposed ahead of the August registration process include Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise and former Riho Ühtegi. Incumbent Alar Karis announced during the midsummer break that he would not be seeking a second term.

Opposition parties cautious

Urmas Reinsalu Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

The most popular and biggest opposition party, Isamaa, said it plans to meet with Laul on Thursday afternoon. Chairman Urmas Reinsalu said the party is open to Laul's possible candidacy.

"Our fundamental position is that we are open to all candidates and all names that have been put forward. Naturally, it is also important to hear Indrek Laul's views on how he intends to fulfil the office of president and how he sees Estonia's current situation, prospects and challenges," he said.

"I think it is a very welcome and symbolic sign of the times that citizens are putting forward candidates for parliament to consider. It is also a very serious step on Indrek Laul's part to be prepared to take on this responsibility, so I view it very positively," Reinsalu said.

On Wednesday, the party met with retired Maj. Gen Riho Ühtegi, who has also put himself forward for the role.

Lauri Läänemets. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

SDE Chairman Lauri Läanemets said the party has no position on Indrek Laul, but it prefers Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise as the candidate.

"We have said that Ülle Madise seems to have the greatest potential for this common ground. The Social Democrats will not start discussing it until Ülle Madise has expressed her final position," he said.

"The Social Democrats have no reason today to abandon their fundamental support for Ülle Madis," the former interior minister confirmed.

However, the chairman said he was pleased that other groups were putting forward their own nominees. "There are worthy people in Estonia, and this is yet another example," he said.

Raimond Kaljulaid. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

SDE MP Raimond Kaljualid said Laul may struggle to find support as a so-called non-system candidate, not proposed by a party.

The MP said Laul's strength is his successful experience in managing international business, but his weakness is his lack of political background.

"Supporting business diplomacy goes hand in hand with the office of president, but it is not the central issue or core of the president's role. Which is why the main argument in favor of Laul is somewhat weaker than that of those with a background in state institutions," Kaljulaid wrote on social media.

However, this does not rule him out completely, he added.

Kaljulaid advised Laul to begin his campaign and meet with members of the Riigikogu and local government leaders. "Whoever starts their campaign earlier and runs it better may ultimately emerge as the winner," he stressed.

This story was updated to add comments from Raimond Kaljulaid, Urmas Reinsalu and Lauri Läänemets

World.title: First Finnish opera cruise brings nearly 900 fans to Saaremaa
World.content:
Hundreds of opera lovers sailed from Finland to Saaremaa this week aboard the island's first opera cruise, combining sightseeing with a performance of Verdi's "La Traviata."

The charter cruise from Helsinki marked the first time a dedicated opera-themed voyage has brought audiences directly to Saaremaa Opera Days.

After arriving aboard the MS Victoria I Wednesday morning, passengers toured Kuressaare before attending a sold-out performance of Giuseppe Verdi's "La Traviata" by the Livorno, Italy-based Goldoni Theater in the courtyard of Kuressaare Castle.

Local guide Annika Tamm said nine buses met the ship at Saaremaa Harbor to take visitors into town, where they explored Kuressaare before the afternoon performance.

Riina Aamisepp, marketing manager for Eesti Kontsert, said organizers had long discussed using the island's deepwater harbor to bring audiences directly to the festival. The dream finally started to become a reality last fall.

"Last November, one of Finland's largest travel agencies, Ikaalisten Matkatoimisto, approached us with the idea," Aamisepp recalled.

The opera cruise's cultural program began even before the ship reached Estonia, as soloists from the Estonian National Opera performed a half-hour concert on board Tuesday evening.

"We put together a lovely half-hour program, and were given a very warm reception," soprano Kadri Raalik said.

Start of a new tradition

Estonian National Opera marketing manager Rein Mikk said there was no doubt the cruise passengers were real opera fans.

"It was a great touch by organizers to bring a musicologist on board to walk the nearly thousand passengers through a deeper look into the story of 'La Traviata,'" Mikk added.

Organizers hope the voyage will become an annual tradition.

Aamisepp said Eesti Kontsert, Ikaalisten Matkatoimisto and Portugal's São Carlos National Theater — next year's featured guest company — are already planning another opera cruise for 2027, with hopes of eventually attracting visitors from Sweden as well.

World.title: Government ministers on vacation
World.content:
The coalition's weekly cabinet meeting and press conference will not take place this week as Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) and four other ministers are on holiday.

The cabinet meeting, where policy is usually shaped and political agreements are reached, but no formal decisions are made, will not take place this week because Prime Minister Kristen Michal is on holiday, the Government Office's communications bureau told ERR.

As a rule, the cabinet meeting is held when the prime minister can attend.

The prime minister is on holiday from July 20 to 29; Minister of Education and Research Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) is on holiday from July 23 to 31; Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa-Ly Pakosta (Eesti 200) is on holiday from July 20 to August 4; Minister of Social Affairs Karmen Joller (Reform) is on holiday from July 14 to 31; and Minister of Infrastructure Kuldar Leis (Reform) is on holiday from July 17 to 24.

The ministers who take part in the government's press conference are selected based on the issues discussed and decided at the government meeting and cabinet meeting.

Ministers whose areas of responsibility are not on the agenda are not normally invited to the press conference.

"As several ministers are on holiday or engaged in other work-related duties during the second half of July, and based on the items discussed at today's meeting it was not possible to assemble the usual line-up of participants for the press conference, it was decided to cancel the press conference this week," the Government Office said.

The government's e-session took place on Thursday via electronic means of communication. The Government Office confirmed that the government's day-to-day work continues as normal.

World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: Ukraine’s new army chief: who is Mykhailo Drapaty?
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky has announced Mykhailo Drapaty as the country’s new commander-in-chief, following a political crisis triggered by Zelensky’s surprise ousting of a young modernising defence minister.

The 43-year-old Drapaty replaces Oleksandr Syrsky, 60, an accomplished military strategist but who was long criticised for Soviet-style practices and not caring about human losses.

Here is what we know about Drapaty.

– Fighting Russian separatists –

Drapaty is a career military officer trained exclusively inside Ukraine’s independent, post-Soviet system.

He began as a lieutenant and rose through the ranks, shooting to nationwide fame during the war with Russia-backed separatists in 2014.

In a video which went viral, he commanded an infantry vehicle as it smashed through a makeshift barricade set up by pro-Moscow forces in the southern city of Mariupol.

Recalling the incident in an interview with Ukrainian media, Drapaty said his driver asked: “Major, there are barricades ahead. What do we do?”

“I said, ‘Dima, step on the gas'”.

The vehicle, with the blue-and-yellow Ukrainian flag affixed to its top, then smashes through the tyre-and-barricade wall, leaping into the air and speeding on.

During the fight with Moscow-backed rebels, Drapaty is also credited with re-capturing several settlements from Russian control and then saving his unit from being encircled.

Drapaty has a wife and kids, Ukrainian media reported.

– Backing army ‘transformation’ –

Drapaty is seen as a consensus candidate and popular choice.

He enjoys a good reputation within the military, and protesters calling for his predecessor’s removal often chanted his name as their preferred replacement.

Despite being well-known, he has kept a low profile and only rarely given interviews — in contrast with many other Ukrainian commanders.

After a string of Russian attacks on Ukrainian training grounds, he resigned from his position as ground forces commander in June 2025 — a move that set him apart as commander willing to take responsibility for mistakes.

“If we fail to draw conclusions, to change our attitude toward service, to acknowledge our mistakes, we are doomed,” he said at the time.

“That episode illustrates his decisiveness and strong ethical standards,” political commentator Volodymyr Fesenko told AFP on Wednesday.

Drapaty was immediately moved to become head of Ukraine’s joint forces command, from where he pushed for reforms inside the system.

After the dismissal of moderniser Fedorov last week, he said the “transformation” of the army must continue.

“When the right decision has to be implemented in spite of the system, rather than because of it, it means that the system itself needs to change,” he said in a rare public intervention.

“The army needs new rules,” he added.

– Hailed as ‘fresh air’ –

His nomination was hailed by many inside and outside the army.

The appointment is “wonderful news”, said Sergiy Prytula, the head of one of Ukraine’s biggest charities supporting the military.

“This is a breath of fresh air and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice,” the ousted defence minister Fedorov, an ally, said on social media.

In Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the change would not impact the course of the war.

“I don’t think this will lead to any changes on the front lines,” he told reporters, adding that Moscow intends to continue pressing on with its almost four-and-a-half-year offensive.

– Facing a ‘very difficult time’ –

Despite Ukraine being in one of its best positions on the front line in months, Drapaty faces serious challenges.

The army has been blighted by several scandals — particularly over an unpopular mobilisation drive, the treatment of conscripts and reports of widespread absenteeism and equipment shortages in some units.

“The new Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine will have a very difficult time. Much harder than he imagines,” former army chief Valery Zaluzhny — removed in 2024 — said.

The public row over the last week has exposed hidden divisions within Ukraine’s military and political leadership.

His appointment, seen as an attempt to bridge the divide, carries heavy expectations.

“Appointments made against a backdrop of social turmoil always come with many pitfalls,” said Prytula, adding that Drapaty now faces “inflated expectations”.

World.title: Iraq signs $200 billion in deals with US energy companies
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that the deals struck with US energy corporations during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States are estimated at $200 billion.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the new agreements will raise Iraq’s oil production capacity, create job opportunities, and help the country achieve self-sufficiency in gas by 2030, according to the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The deals include agreements with HKN Energy, Chevron, and Halliburton to develop the oilfields of Hamrin, West Qurna-2, Nasiriyah, Balad, Bin Omar, and Sindbad, as well as an agreement with Syria to construct the Haditha-Baniyas oil pipeline.

Khudair noted that Iraq’s current oil production capacity is 4.8 million barrels per day, but the government is in serious discussions with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to increase oil exports.

Just like most other oil producers, Iraq has to face the issue of how to attract investments and increase production under the restrictions imposed by OPEC.

Despite having some of the world’s greatest crude oil reserves, ongoing production constraints impede Iraq’s efforts to generate revenues needed to support its growing population.

World.title: Offline maps, LoRa devices and tear gas hacks: Jantar Mantar protest survival tips trend online
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party continued at Jantar Mantar amid repeated clashes with police, social media has been flooded with "survival guides" offering tips on coping with internet shutdowns, tear gas exposure and police action.

From downloading offline maps and using Bluetooth-based messaging apps to carrying antacid solutions for tear gas exposure, demonstrators are increasingly relying on crowdsourced advice to navigate the ongoing agitation.

One social media user, who said he had been stranded during repeated internet shutdowns at the protest site, advised participants to download offline maps before arriving. He also recommended installing Bluetooth-based messaging applications that function without mobile data or WiFi, enabling communication even during connectivity disruptions.

The user further suggested installing locally run large language models (LLMs) that operate directly on devices instead of cloud-based AI services, allowing access to AI tools even when internet services are suspended.

He also advised protesters to carry LoRa-based communication devices, which can enable long-range communication when mobile networks are unavailable, and urged them to save the contact details of at least five people living near the protest venue to use in emergencies.





Advice on dealing with tear gas has also gained traction online. A social media user recommended carrying a mixture of equal parts water and an antacid such as Maalox or Digene, claiming it could help reduce the burning sensation and eye irritation caused by tear gas exposure. She said she shared the remedy after a friend found it useful during an earlier protest.

Another protester said he carried a painter's mask or an ordinary dust mask along with protective goggles to reduce exposure to smoke and chemical irritants.

Some demonstrators have also devised makeshift protective gear against baton charges. One protester said he placed thermocol sheets inside his jeans around the back and hip area to provide cushioning. He added that he carried a spare shirt for himself and a kurta for any female protester in case someone's clothes were torn during the demonstration.

The protester also said he carried two helmets, one for himself and another to lend to anyone who needed protection.

The trend reflects how demonstrators are increasingly turning to social media for practical advice and real-time information during the protests.

On Monday, several students and other protesters were injured in clashes with police during their march to Parliament. One woman was rushed to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in critical condition. Several police personnel were also injured in the confrontations.

The students, protesting under the banner of the Cockroach Janata Party, have been demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak controversy.

World.title: 30,000-ft health scare: British Airways launches probe after 3 pilots suffer food poisoning on Hyderabad-London flight
World.content:
30,000-ft health scare: British Airways launches probe after 3 pilots suffer food poisoning on Hyderabad-London flight

NEW DELHI: Three British Airways pilots operating a flight from Hyderabad to London fell ill after suspected food poisoning, prompting the airline to launch an investigation into the incident. One of the pilots became incapacitated while the aircraft was cruising at 30,000 feet and required oxygen and urgent medical treatment after landing.The incident occurred on British Airways flight BA276, which departed Hyderabad for London Heathrow after the crew's overnight stopover in the city.According to Gulf News, the three pilots had breakfast together at a hotel lounge in Hyderabad before the flight. However, they reportedly consumed bottled water supplied by an external company.The first pilot became seriously unwell during the flight and was unable to continue normal duties. The other two pilots completed the journey safely, although their condition reportedly worsened as the flight progressed.The aircraft landed safely in London without any reported operational issues.British Airways has confirmed the incident and said it is reviewing the crew's accommodation arrangements in Hyderabad."The welfare of our colleagues is a top priority, and we are reviewing crew accommodation in this location following some isolated reports of sickness," the airline said in a statement.All three pilots have filed Air Safety Reports and were asked to provide medical samples to help doctors identify the source of the illness.The incident is considered highly unusual because commercial airlines follow strict safety protocols designed to prevent all members of the flight deck crew from becoming ill at the same time. These measures often include encouraging or requiring pilots to eat different meals.Food poisoning has long been recognised as a potential aviation safety risk and is one of the reasons airlines maintain strict crew meal policies.British Airways has faced similar incidents in the past. In 1984, a major food poisoning outbreak affected nearly 1,000 passengers, crew members and ground staff, disrupting the airline's global operations. More recently, in 2024, a United Airlines flight from Incheon to San Francisco returned to South Korea after several pilots and cabin crew members became ill shortly after take-off, according to Arabian Business.

World.title: Mamata passes Martyrs' Day street test; marathon begins now
World.content:
On 20th July night,

refused to leave the Martyrs' Day stage after her faction alleged that it had been vandalised. Less than two weeks earlier, a protest march led by her had been disrupted by clashes with people the

identified as BJP workers. A veteran politician that she is, Mamata refused to take another chance and kept a night-long vigil.

There was something faintly Shakespearean about the scene, a former ruler separated from the machinery of her kingdom, surrounded by a diminished circle of loyalists and guarding a stage her faction said had been vandalised.

By the next afternoon, she was back on stage, speaking largely extempore. There were fewer people to thank, with the guest list missing its usual glamour quotient, and fewer formalities to observe.

The poetry was not as eloquent as in the past. Her Hindi was toned down, now that Delhi was no longer calling. The plans she laid out were not grandiose; in fact, they were skeletal, reflecting a fear of further backstabbing.

Yet Didi was in her element, refusing to throw in the towel without a fight.

For TMC workers, Mamata remains the agni-kanya, the leader who can blaze through opposition by sheer force of action. But this July 21 was an acid test.





After the May 4 defeat and the desertion of a large part of the partyâs rank and file, Mamata had to prove to her detractors, and perhaps to herself, that she could still draw a crowd without the full weight of the well-oiled party machinery or the organisational muscle of many of her former lieutenants.

By that limited yardstick, Mamata passed with flying colours.

The breakaway faction cut a sorry figure, with a TOI report citing a

, far below Mamataâs gathering. The

, which held its own Martyrsâ Day observance, surprisingly managed to cobble together a reasonable gathering.

This was no longer the old Dharmatala sea. But Mamata still occupied the largest space.

Congress commemorating Martyrs Day

What happened on July 21?

Martyrsâ Day commemorates 12 Youth Congress workers who were killed in police firing during a procession towards Writersâ Buildings on July 21, 1993. A 13th participant remains missing and is commemorated alongside them. The march was led by Mamata Banerjee and, significantly, the demand was for mandatory photo identity cards for voters.

A commission report recently tabled in the state assembly described the firing as âworse than the Jallianwala Bagh massacreâ.

Former registrar of Calcutta University and professor in the Department of South and Southeast Asian Studies at the same university, Dr Raja Gopal Dhar Chakrabarti, speaking to TOI, recalls that fateful day in 1993, when he believes Mamata protested against âLeftist anarchyâ. The frenzy in the crowd was maddening, and many who wanted to join the protest could not reach the venue, he reminisces.

According to Chakrabarti, who has diligently tracked the day since then, July 21 has, over the years, morphed into something much bigger. Mamata completely appropriated the event even after leaving the Congress and virtually turned it into the TMCâs annual political day. It measured not merely popular support but organisational obedience. This year, ironically, July 21 became a test of who represented the real TMC.

The martyrsâ families, too, remained divided, with members of some families attending the Ritabrata Banerjee-led Trinamool event and others choosing Mamataâs programme. But the loyalty of those who mattered politically appeared to rest firmly with the Kalighat camp.

Some martyrs family went to Mamata's event, others attended Ritabrata's.

Speaking to TOI, political analyst and former Vidyasagar University vice-chancellor Dr.Sibaji Pratim Basu says that Mamata was never short of charisma, right from her early days.

This yearâs Martyrsâ Day merely reiterated that she still retains the ability to be a natural crowd-puller. Chakrabarti believes that, compared with Mamataâs heyday, this yearâs July 21 was a much more tepid affair, but she undoubtedly managed to establish that support remains with her.

In the assembly election, the TMC won 80 seats, polling 40.8% of the votes and falling 32.1 lakh votes short of the BJPâs overall tally of 2.92 crore.

Thus, while the party received a royal thrashing, fuelled largely by anti-incumbency, its core vote bank remains robust.

A lot of water has flowed down the Hooghly since May. The TMC has effectively broken into three parts, with the NCPI parliamentary bloc and the Ritabrata faction splintering from the original party. The NCPI bloc, fronted by

Sudip Bandyopadhyay

and Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, has abandoned even the fig leaf of anti-BJP mobilisation that the MLAs led by Ritabrata continue to maintain in Kolkata. A large number of legislators have left Mamataâs camp, with her trusted aide

Madan Mitra

among the latest defectors. The precise strength of the competing factions remains contested, but the Mamata-led TMC is undoubtedly a much smaller political entity than it was immediately after the election.

NCPI bloc at Rajghat

With future municipal and panchayat contests looming, its organisational presence could be squeezed further if Bengalâs earlier political pattern repeats itself. In that context, July 21 acquired additional importance. It was virtually a referendum in the peopleâs court.

Reaching for the old playbook

During her fiery speech, Mamata also doubled down on Abhishek Banerjeeâs position in the party hierarchy. At the same time, she reached for tricks from her old playbook that made old-timers fondly turn back the clock by two decades.

In 2004 and 2006, the TMC suffered two devastating electoral jolts. The backfiring of the âIndia Shiningâ campaign in 2004 meant that NDA ally TMC was reduced to a solitary Lok Sabha seat. In the 2006 assembly election, the party was obliterated, slumping to only 30 seats. Many had written Mamataâs political obituary. However, she rose like a phoenix, aided by some luck, the CPI(M)âs complacent governance and mounting anti-incumbency.

But nothing came to her on a platter.

What happened on July 21

Political observers who closely followed the TMCâs rise during that period recall how Mamata, alongside Mukul Roy, took the long and arduous route of rebuilding the organisation through small meetings in the districts. She rode pillion on a motorcycle to reach places where ordinary people had been affected. Both the Singur and Nandigram movements could have fizzled out if not for her sustained campaigns.

The focus on returning to the grassroots, pun intended, was reiterated by the former chief minister this time as well.

According to Basu, Mamata managed to break the perception that the CPI(M) was the party of the poor and went on to become the toast of the subalterns. But this time, the competition is more formidable. However, Basu believes that the BJPâs honeymoon period has been incredibly short, although nothing will change on the ground before the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.

Chakrabarti, too, echoes similar sentiments about the mood already souring against the BJP, especially over the mass deletions from the Annapurna scheme, and believes Mamata can become a strong challenger again.

Taking the long route

That is where the real test begins. With Bengalâs history of giving incumbents a long rope, her work is cut out for her. Rebuilding the organisation across 294 constituencies is a physically taxing proposition, believes Chakrabarti.

Most importantly, who will play the role of Mukul Roy, silently building the organisation and ironing out the rough edges? Roy had largely controlled the organisation during Mamataâs first term and was once described by party insiders as the leader who could run it almost single-handedly. Abhishek Banerjeeâs often flashy style of politics is not for the faint-hearted. It is more T20, whereas the need is perhaps for a good old-fashioned Test-match grind.

Across Bengal, the TMC lost ground amid concerns over corruption, shoddy governance and the conduct of local leaders. According to Mamata, the corrupt have now left and there is nothing to worry about. That may energise those who stayed. It is not, by itself, an adequate diagnosis of defeat. But Basu believes Mamata still largely retains, among her supporters, the image of being untouched by the stench of corruption, which works in her favour.

According to Chakrabarti, Mamata can regain traction but has to be careful about using Abhishek Banerjee. The noted political commentator is of the opinion that leaders may be sceptical about rejoining the TMC if Abhishek continues to be such a vital cog in the wheel.

Mamata has, for now, firmly shut the door on those who deserted the party. She also unequivocally backed Abhishek, even asking workers to contact the MP if the need arose.

Madan Mitra, speaking from the opposition camp, gave Mamata one month to âleave Abhishekâs handâ if she wanted the leaders back. Mamata, though, appears to be in no mood for reconciliation. She also issued a warning to Suvendu Adhikari, suggesting that she could reveal what he had done during his years as a TMC minister.

A new alliance arithmetic?

Another interesting facet of Mamataâs speech was her courting of INDIA bloc partners. This was in sharp contrast to her pre-election attitude, when the then chief minister, harbouring larger ambitions, was in no mood to give any ground to either the Congress or the Left.

Circumstances have changed, and so has Mamataâs outreach. But will the Congress and the Left play ball? For the Left, the distance may be too great for it to hobnob with the party that displaced it and subsequently occupied much of its political space.

For the Congress, however, the TMC remains a more natural ally.

Mamataâs prominent photographs at the Congressâs Shahid Minar observance amounted to more than a subtle overture.

The Congress used images of her role in the 1993 movement even while accusing the TMC of later turning Martyrsâ Day into a political instrument. It is no secret that the Congress high command has often been warmer towards Mamata than its state leadership. But with Mamata cut to size, the Congress could now seek a far more equitable arrangement in any future alliance.

According to Chakrabarti, Muslims are unlikely to ever move towards the BJP.

The educated among them may veer towards Naushad Siddiqui of the ISF, but the rest would choose between the TMC and the Congress. Thus, a future tie-up is very much within the realm of possibility.



The rebelsâ narrowing road

For the breakaway faction, July 21 was a brutal reality check. Whatever the reasons behind its desertion of the mothership, it is undeniable that most of its leaders originally won because of Mamataâs support. Their options are narrowing.

Returning would require Mamata to reopen a door she has publicly bolted. Contesting independently would require them to build a political identity that does not yet exist. Moving closer to the BJP would expose the hollowness of their continuing anti-BJP position.

According to Basu, very few would be trusted even by the BJP because of what he describes as their political deceit.

Chakrabarti is even more blunt in his assessment, saying that Ritabrata and the members of his rebel team have no future.

The political scientist remains flummoxed about what exactly may have forced the likes of Firhad Hakim to cross over. What will keep Mamata worried is that even on July 21, there was a reported public bust-up with Kalyan Banerjee, who left the stage after a brief exchange. The TMC MP denied that there had been an altercation, but the episode nevertheless fed perceptions of continuing tension within the Kalighat camp.

Kalyan Banerjee addressing the crowd

It may have been a small disagreement over speaking time. But the message it sent out may be much graver.



Beyond the street show

Most of those in the crowd appeared to have come on their own, driven by their love for Didi. Leaders such as Madan Mitra and Anubrata Mondal, who had once helped oversee the partyâs district mobilisation, are now in the rival camp. But elections require ample funds and organisational heft, not merely the fervent zeal of the dedicated.

That is where the TMC will encounter its next big challenge.

At the meeting, there was repeated emphasis on Mamata having groomed generations of leaders and on her faith in the youth. But the ledger of the past must be reconciled before the future is planned. Beyond the usual rhetoric of the BJP stealing the election, the TMC needs honest introspection about why it was ousted from power. If the leadership knew about corruption, why did it not act? What will it do differently if the public gives it another chance?

According to Raja Gopal Dhar Chakrabarti, the difference between 2006 and 2026 is that, at the time, she was the challenger and people thought highly of her potential, irrespective of the electoral outcome. Now, after three terms in power, the novelty factor has worn off, and few may be willing to give her a second chance very soon.

The physical demands of the intense running around needed to rebuild the party may also be extremely taxing for Mamata, Chakrabarti believes. Sibaji Pratim Basu disagrees and cites present Prime Minister

Narendra Modi

and Morarji Desai as examples of leaders who managed to dominate Indian politics at a more advanced age. July 21 showed that Mamata Banerjee can still own the street. It demonstrated that she is still up for a good political fight. For one afternoon, that was enough. Political resurrection, however, will be a long, tedious path. At 71, Mamata Banerjee will have to run the marathon again. Does she have the stamina for the long haul?

Time will tell.

World.title: 'Jantar Mantar not the place for you': BJP's Nishikant Dubey urges protesting students to focus on studies
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Thursday appealed to students protesting over the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar to return to their studies, saying education, not agitation, was the path to achieving careers in medicine, engineering and the civil services.

He also called for a stringent law against paper leaks, suggesting that Parliament could even provide for the death penalty for those responsible.

Addressing protesting students in Delhi, Dubey said, "Jantar Mantar is not the place for you. If you want to get into medical colleges, engineering colleges, or become an IAS or IPS officer, you have to go to the path of education and focus on your studies. In 1975, there was a students' movement, and among the students who participated in that agitation, many could not become doctors or engineers for two years.

The situation became such that they did become leaders - some became Chief Ministers and others achieved political positions- but the dream their parents had, of seeing them become doctors or professionals, could not be fulfilled because they left their studies.

.."

In a post on X, Dubey also urged students to prioritise academics over protests, writing, "Students should study. This movement will not let you complete your education."





Backing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for strict action against those involved in paper leaks, the BJP MP said the government was committed to ensuring the harshest punishment for the accused.

"The PM clearly said that top lawyers will be hired against the 13 arrested people, and they should be given the harshest punishmentâ¦all parents want to send their children to top institutions believing they excel in studies, but some children want to use paper leaks as an excuse trying to convince their parents that they are very good at studies but cannot compete solely because the paper gets leakedâ¦if anyone wants to go to a medical or engineering college, or become an IAS or IPS officer, you must go through the door of educationâ¦"

Dubey also urged opposition parties to allow a discussion in Parliament on the issue, saying a tougher legal framework was needed to tackle examination fraud.

"If the Opposition will allow a discussion in the House, just as the strong law that came for women after the Nirbhaya murder case, similarly, we can provide for a strong punishment provision in the case of paper leaks. Rahul Gandhi is not concerned for the students."

In another post on X, Dubey suggested that Parliament could enact a law prescribing the death penalty for those found guilty of leaking examination papers.

"If Parliament convenes, a law can be enacted to ensure that those who leak exam papers receive punishment up to the death penalty."

World.title: Parliament standoff: Government reaches out to opposition for NEET debate, urges talks without preconditions
World.content: NEW DELHI: The government is reaching out to the opposition leaders to break the deadlock in Parliament over the NEET paper leak issue, government sources told news agency ANI on Thursday. This is a fresh effort from the government's side to end the repeated disruptions that have stalled proceedings through the first week of the Monsoon session.According to government sources, the Centre has conveyed to opposition parties that it is ready for a discussion on the alleged NEET paper leak but wants the debate to take place "without any preconditions", including the opposition's demand for the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The government is also likely to convene a meeting of floor leaders soon in an attempt to build consensus on holding the discussion, the sources said.The outreach comes amid a continuing impasse in Parliament, where proceedings have been repeatedly disrupted over the issue.Earlier in the day, Union home minister Amit Shah met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla after the House was adjourned amid sustained protests by opposition members.Before Shah's meeting with the Speaker, leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress MPs Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra were among the opposition leaders who met Birla.During Question Hour, the Speaker had asked opposition leaders to meet him to discuss the duration and scheduling of a debate on the NEET paper leak issue.The government has maintained that it is prepared for a discussion but has accused the opposition of insisting on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as a condition for participating in the debate. Opposition parties have been demanding accountability over the alleged examination irregularities and have pressed for the minister to step down.The Monsoon session, which began on Monday, has witnessed repeated adjournments as opposition parties protested over the NEET paper leak and the alleged theft of donations from the Ram temple. Police action against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protests in Delhi has also figured prominently in the opposition's protests inside Parliament.

World.title: Water cannon, tug of war and a stolen gate: Patna NEET protest goes viral
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Students protesting the NEET paper leak in Patna turned a tense demonstration into a viral moment, when they asked police to use water cannons because of the heat, and then danced as officers sprayed them.

The protest, organised by the All India Students' Association, an affiliate of CPI(ML) Liberation, demanded the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination irregularities. As marchers made their way towards Raj Bhavan, police set up barricades near Gandhi Maidan, about three kilometres from the Governor's residence.

Protest clips go viral

In a video that has since gone viral, students can be heard telling police: "Sir, do you not have arrangements for a water cannon, it's too hot here."

Police responded by spraying water at the crowd. Rather than taking cover, many students began dancing on the spot, a moment social media users have now made viral.

Other viral moments from the protest showed students playing tug of war with police rope. In another clip, protesters were seen picking up and running away with police barricades meant to block them. There were also reports of students unscrewing a gate and taking it with them.





The clip triggered a wave of jokes and memes online. One widely shared comment read, "E Jantar Mantar nahin hai babu, ye Bihar hai" â "This isn't Delhi's Jantar Mantar, sir, this is Bihar." Another quipped that experiencing tear gas would now require "a trip to Delhi." Some even compared the scene to a Holi celebration.

A BJP leader arrived at the protest site in Patna to disrupt the demonstration. Students recognised him from the flag he was holding and beat him.
